nodes.description: How much water passes through each point — the basis of streams and erosion patterns

attrs.label: Logarithmic
attrs.tooltip:
Accumulation spans several orders of magnitude — a few
channels carry almost everything. Without this the map
is black with a handful of bright lines.

attrs.label: Channel threshold
attrs.tooltip:
Discards everything below this fraction, leaving only
the established channels.

attrs.label: Route through basins
attrs.tooltip:
Water that reaches a hollow fills it and flows on.
Off follows the raw surface, where every stream stops
at the first pit it meets.

attrs.label: Remap to range
attrs.tooltip:
Rescales the result so its lowest point sits at the
bottom of the range below and its highest at the top.
Off keeps the raw values, which is what you want when
a node feeds arithmetic rather than a picture.

attrs.label: Output range
attrs.tooltip:
The low and high the result is rescaled into. 0..1 is
the terrain's own range; a narrower band makes this
node a gentler contribution when it is added to
another.

attrs.label: Invert
attrs.tooltip:
Turns the result upside down within its range - peaks
become hollows. Applied after the remap.

attrs.label: Gain (gamma)
attrs.tooltip:
Bends the result toward its low or high end. Below 1
lifts the middle, so more of the map sits high; above
1 pushes it down, so peaks become sparser and sharper.

attrs.label: Zero edges width
attrs.tooltip:
Fades the terrain to zero at the borders over this
fraction of the map — clean edges for islands/tiles.

attrs.label: Invert blend
attrs.tooltip:
Applies this node where the blend input is dark instead of
where it is bright.

nodes.description: Height relative to the neighborhood

attrs.label: Radius (px)
attrs.tooltip:
How far out the surrounding ground is sampled before
asking how high this point stands above it. Small radii
find local bumps; large ones find whether you are on a
ridge or in a valley at all.

nodes.description: Rebuilds the terrain at a coarser or finer sampling — detail control, not size

attrs.label: Sampling
attrs.tooltip:
Coarser sampling discards fine detail, which is how you
get a smooth base to build on. Finer sampling cannot
invent detail — it interpolates.

attrs.label: Custom size
attrs.tooltip:
The size to resample to, when Custom is chosen above.
Resampling changes how much detail a buffer can hold
without changing the graph's own resolution.

attrs.label: Smooth interpolation
attrs.tooltip:
Off: nearest neighbour, which keeps hard edges and gives
a deliberately blocky, terraced look.

nodes.description: How much of the sky each point can see - open ridges near 1, valley floors shut in by their own walls near 0

attrs.label: Directions
attrs.tooltip:
How many compass directions the horizon is measured in.
Each one is a single linear pass over the terrain, so the
cost is flatly proportional to this: 8 is enough for a
soft ambient look, 32 for hard terrain shadows that have
to line up with the sun.

attrs.label: Vertical scale
attrs.tooltip:
The terrain's height range as a fraction of the tile's
width - 0.25 means a kilometre of ground rising 250 m.
This is what turns the heightmap into real angles, so
match it to the scene's own vertical scale or the
shadows will be too long or too short.

nodes.description: How much direct sun reaches each point - the ground a ridge keeps in shadow all day, which is where the snow stays

attrs.label: Sun azimuth
attrs.tooltip:
Which way the sun lies, in degrees around the
compass: 0 north, 90 east, 180 south, 270 west. Match
it to the scene's sun and the shadows agree with the
render.

attrs.label: Sun altitude
attrs.tooltip:
How high the sun stands above the horizon, in
degrees. Low sun throws long shadows and picks out
every fold in the ground; overhead sun shadows almost
nothing.

attrs.label: Sweep
attrs.tooltip:
How far the sun travels, in degrees of azimuth, and
the result is the fraction of that journey each point
is lit for. Zero is one instant - a hard shadow map.
Ninety is a morning, and gives the soft edges you
want for deciding where snow survives rather than
where a shadow falls right now.

nodes.description: Surface statistics: rugosity, TRI, shape index

attrs.label: Metric
attrs.tooltip:
Which statistic is measured. Rugosity is surface area
against footprint - how crumpled the ground is. TRI is the
average height difference to the neighbours, which finds
broken ground. Shape index separates domes from hollows.

attrs.label: Radius (px)
attrs.tooltip:
How far the measurement reaches. Small radii describe the
surface texture; large ones describe the landform.

nodes.description: Where water collects — high in flat hollows fed from above, low on steep ground

attrs.label: Minimum slope
attrs.tooltip:
Perfectly flat ground would divide by zero and give an
infinitely wet pixel. This is the flattest slope the
index will consider.

attrs.label: Contrast
attrs.tooltip:
Stretches the wetness values apart. The raw index is
bunched into a narrow band, so without this most of the
map reads as the same dampness.

Frames rendered per second of the sequence. This decides

attrs.label: Sweep the sun
attrs.tooltip:

cycle without keyframing anything.

attrs.label: Sun from: azimuth °

attrs.label: Sun to: azimuth °

nodes.description: A wave of time: sine, triangle, square or sawtooth, for anything that should pulse

attrs.label: Waveform
attrs.tooltip: The wave the value follows over time.

attrs.label: Frequency (Hz)
attrs.tooltip: How many cycles a second.

attrs.label: Phase
attrs.tooltip:
Where in the cycle it starts, as a fraction of one cycle.
Use it to run two oscillators out of step.

attrs.label: Amplitude
attrs.tooltip: How far the value swings either side of the offset.

attrs.label: Offset
attrs.tooltip: The value the wave is centred on.

nodes.description: Speeds, offsets, loops or ping-pongs time before it reaches a graph

attrs.label: Speed
attrs.tooltip:
How fast time runs for everything downstream. Negative
runs it backwards.

attrs.label: Offset (s)
attrs.tooltip:
Shifts time before it reaches the graph, so a downstream
animation starts earlier or later without moving its keys.

attrs.label: Loop length (s, 0 = none)
attrs.tooltip: The length of time after which it repeats. 0 never loops.

attrs.label: Ping-pong
attrs.tooltip: With a loop length: run forward then backward instead of jumping.

nodes.description: Sky colors, density, haze/fog and light absorption

attrs.label: Atmosphere density
attrs.tooltip:
How thick the air is. It reddens the sun near the horizon
and washes distance out to blue - the single strongest cue
of scale in a landscape, because it tells the eye how far
away a ridge is.

attrs.label: Ambient light
attrs.tooltip:
How much light the sky itself throws down. This is what
fills the shadows; too little and they read as black holes
rather than shade.

attrs.label: Zenith R
attrs.tooltip:
The red component of the sky straight overhead, linear
rather than sRGB.

attrs.label: Zenith G
attrs.tooltip:
The green component of the sky straight overhead, linear
rather than sRGB.

attrs.label: Zenith B
attrs.tooltip:
The blue component of the sky straight overhead, linear
rather than sRGB.

attrs.label: Horizon R
attrs.tooltip:
The red component of the sky at the horizon, linear rather
than sRGB.

attrs.label: Horizon G
attrs.tooltip:
The green component of the sky at the horizon, linear
rather than sRGB.

attrs.label: Horizon B
attrs.tooltip:
The blue component of the sky at the horizon, linear
rather than sRGB.

attrs.label: Fog type
Fog density
attrs.tooltip: How thick the fog is.

attrs.label: Fog level
attrs.tooltip:
The height the fog sits at, for the height-based kinds.
Below it the air is thick, above it clear.

attrs.label: Vertical falloff
attrs.tooltip:
How quickly the fog thins above its level. Sharp gives a
defined top surface with peaks standing out of it; soft
gives a haze that fades away.

attrs.label: Fog R
attrs.tooltip: The red component of the fog, linear rather than sRGB.

attrs.label: Fog G
attrs.tooltip: The green component of the fog, linear rather than sRGB.

attrs.label: Fog B
attrs.tooltip: The blue component of the fog, linear rather than sRGB.

attrs.label: Sun scattering
attrs.tooltip:
How much the fog glows toward the sun. This is what makes
looking into a misty sunrise bright and looking away from
it flat, and without it fog reads as grey paint.

nodes.description: Volumetric cloud layer: type, coverage, altitude, wind

attrs.label: Enabled
attrs.tooltip: Turns the cloud layer off without losing its settings.

attrs.label: Cloud type
attrs.tooltip:
The kind of cloud. Each has its own shape and altitude
behaviour - flat sheets, heaped cumulus, high wisps.

attrs.label: Coverage
attrs.tooltip: 0 = clear sky, 1 = solid overcast.

attrs.label: Density
attrs.tooltip:
How opaque the cloud is. Thin lets the sun through and
lights the cloud from within; thick blocks it and casts
shadow on the ground.

attrs.label: Base altitude
attrs.tooltip: How high the layer sits.

attrs.label: Thickness
attrs.tooltip:
How deep the layer is from base to top. Depth is what lets
a cloud be lit brightly on top and dark underneath.

attrs.label: Detail erosion
attrs.tooltip:
How much fine structure the cloud has. Low gives soft
blobs; high gives the wispy, torn edges of real cloud.

attrs.label: Anvil spread
attrs.tooltip:
How far the cloud spreads out at its top, the way a storm
cell flattens against the top of the troposphere.

attrs.label: Wind speed
attrs.tooltip:
How fast the layer drifts. Cloud is the only thing in a
still landscape that moves, so this is what makes a
sequence read as time passing.

attrs.label: Wind direction
attrs.tooltip: Which way the layer drifts.

attrs.label: Sky light
attrs.tooltip:
How much sky light the cloud picks up where the sun does
not reach it directly, which sets how dark its underside
goes.

attrs.label: Color R
attrs.tooltip: The red component of the cloud, linear rather than sRGB.

attrs.label: Color G
attrs.tooltip: The green component of the cloud, linear rather than sRGB.

attrs.label: Color B
attrs.tooltip: The blue component of the cloud, linear rather than sRGB.

attrs.label: Quality
attrs.tooltip:
How many samples the raymarcher takes through the cloud.
This is the direct trade between how solid the cloud looks
and how fast the frame draws.

nodes.description: Sun: direction (manual or geographic), color, intensity

attrs.label: Direction mode
attrs.tooltip:
Whether the sun is placed by hand, or worked out from a
place and a time. By date and time is what you want when
the shot has to match a real location and hour.

attrs.label: Azimuth
attrs.tooltip: Which way the sun lies, in degrees around the compass.

attrs.label: Altitude
attrs.tooltip:
How high the sun stands above the horizon. Low light is
long shadows and warm colour; overhead is short shadows
and flat ground.

attrs.label: Latitude
attrs.tooltip:
Where on the earth the scene is, north or south. With the
date and hour this decides where the sun actually sits.

attrs.label: Longitude
attrs.tooltip: Where on the earth the scene is, east or west.

attrs.label: UTC offset
attrs.tooltip: The time zone, so the hour below means local clock time.

attrs.label: Month
attrs.tooltip:
The month, which sets how high the sun can climb at this
latitude.

attrs.label: Day
attrs.tooltip: The day of the month.

attrs.label: Local time
attrs.tooltip: The hour of the day, local time.

attrs.label: Intensity
attrs.tooltip: How bright the sun is.

attrs.label: Color R
attrs.tooltip:
The red component of the sunlight, linear rather than
sRGB.

attrs.label: Color G
attrs.tooltip:
The green component of the sunlight, linear rather than
sRGB.

attrs.label: Color B
attrs.tooltip:
The blue component of the sunlight, linear rather than
sRGB.

attrs.label: Cast shadows
attrs.tooltip:
Whether the sun casts shadows. Turning them off is a great
deal faster and makes the terrain's form much harder to
read.

attrs.label: Level
attrs.tooltip: The height the water surface sits at.

attrs.label: Clarity
attrs.tooltip:
How far light travels into the water before it is
absorbed. Clear water shows the bed in the shallows and
goes deep blue further out; murky water hides the bed at
once.

attrs.label: Opacity
attrs.tooltip: How much the surface hides what is beneath it.

attrs.label: Deep R
attrs.tooltip: The red component of deep water, linear rather than sRGB.

attrs.label: Deep G
attrs.tooltip:
The green component of deep water, linear rather than

attrs.label: Deep B
attrs.tooltip: The blue component of deep water, linear rather than sRGB.

attrs.label: Shallow R
attrs.tooltip:
The red component of shallow water, linear rather than
sRGB.

attrs.label: Shallow G
attrs.tooltip:
The green component of shallow water, linear rather than
sRGB.

attrs.label: Shallow B
attrs.tooltip:
The blue component of shallow water, linear rather than
sRGB.

attrs.label: Wave amplitude
attrs.tooltip: How high the waves stand.

attrs.label: Wave scale
attrs.tooltip:
How far apart the waves are. Together with the height this
is what sets the apparent size of the body of water: small
close-set waves read as a pond however wide it is.

attrs.label: Wave speed
attrs.tooltip: How fast the waves travel.

attrs.label: Foam
attrs.tooltip: Turns foam on at the shoreline and the wave crests.

attrs.label: Shoreline foam
attrs.tooltip: How much foam there is.

attrs.label: Crest foam
attrs.tooltip:
How much foam appears on the wave tops as against at the
shore. Open water foams on its crests; a beach foams where
the water meets the land.

attrs.label: Foam scale
attrs.tooltip: How fine the foam's own texture is.

attrs.tooltip:
The lens, in millimetres on this sensor. Short is wide and

attrs.label: Aperture f/
attrs.tooltip:
The f-number. It sets the depth of field and, with the

much the corners fall off.

attrs.tooltip:
The shutter speed, as 1/x seconds. Slower is brighter and

attrs.label: ISO
attrs.tooltip:
The sensor's sensitivity. Higher is brighter for the same
aperture and shutter.

attrs.tooltip: Index into the film stock list (see the Camera properties).
