attrs.label: Scale
attrs.tooltip: How many fissures cross the terrain.

attrs.label: Wander
attrs.tooltip: Makes the fissures meander instead of running straight.

nodes.description: Loose debris that gathers on slopes and leaves flats clean

attrs.label: Amount
attrs.tooltip: How much debris is laid down.

attrs.label: Grain size
attrs.tooltip: How coarse the debris is, in repeats across the tile.

attrs.label: Slope bias
attrs.tooltip:
How strongly the debris prefers steep ground.
0 spreads it evenly, high values keep it on slopes.

nodes.description: Fine random bumps and holes over the whole surface

attrs.label: Amount
attrs.tooltip: Bump height as a fraction of the terrain's own range.

attrs.label: Grain size
attrs.tooltip: Higher values give finer, denser grain.

nodes.description: Lifts high ground and digs the valleys deeper

attrs.label: Strength
attrs.tooltip:
How far the high ground is lifted and the low ground
pushed down. This exaggerates the relief that is already
there rather than adding new shapes.

attrs.label: Pivot altitude
attrs.tooltip:
Ground above this rises, ground below sinks.
Lower it to keep more of the terrain high.

nodes.description: Makes steep ground steeper — crisp ridges and crests

attrs.label: Amount
attrs.tooltip:
How much local contrast is added. It steepens what is
already steep, so ridges come to a crest instead of a
rounded top.

attrs.label: Radius
attrs.tooltip: Size of the detail that gets emphasized.

attrs.label: Steep areas only
attrs.tooltip:
0 sharpens everything evenly; higher values leave
flat ground untouched.

nodes.description: Clip altitudes — flat tops above, holes below

attrs.label: Clip range
attrs.tooltip:
Ground below the low mark is cut away, ground above
the high mark is flattened. Normalized altitudes.

attrs.label: Below low mark
attrs.tooltip:
What happens below the low mark. Flatten gives a level
floor - a salt pan or a lake bed. Cut away removes the
ground entirely, which is how you punch a hole through the
terrain.

attrs.label: Above high mark
attrs.tooltip:
What happens above the high mark. Flatten cuts the summits
off level, which is what makes a mesa or a plateau out of
a hill.

attrs.label: Edge softness
attrs.tooltip: Blends the cut instead of leaving a hard step.

nodes.description: Mould the ground to the objects standing on it - flat under each, blended around it

attrs.label: Footprints
attrs.tooltip:
Written by the studio from the objects placed on the
terrain (Properties > Ground). One per line: base sink
margin blend, then the base's convex hull.

attrs.label: Blend width
attrs.tooltip:
How far around an object the ground responds, as a
multiple of the footprint's radius - for objects that
do not set their own blend distance.

attrs.label: Smoothness
attrs.tooltip:
The shape of the blend: 0 is a firm shoulder, 1 a long
soft tail.

attrs.label: Keep relief
attrs.tooltip:
How much of the terrain's own small relief survives
inside the blend, so the mould still looks like the
same ground.

attrs.label: Flatten under
attrs.tooltip: How flat the ground is made inside the footprint itself.

attrs.label: Strength
attrs.tooltip: Dial the whole effect back without losing it.

nodes.description: Hand-sculpted layer — brush strokes kept separate from the procedural terrain

attrs.label: Sculpted relief
attrs.tooltip:
Painted in the viewport with the Terrain Editor brushes.
Stored with the project; erasing it resets the sculpt.

attrs.label: Strength
attrs.tooltip:
Scales the whole sculpted layer — dial your edits
back without losing them.

attrs.label: Soften
attrs.tooltip:
Blurs the sculpted layer only, leaving the terrain
underneath crisp.

nodes.description: Coastal shaping: flat beach band, wave planation, bluff

attrs.label: Water level
attrs.tooltip:
The sea level, as a fraction of the terrain's range.
Everything this node does is measured from it.

attrs.label: Beach height band
attrs.tooltip:
Heights within this band above water are planed
into a gently sloping beach.

attrs.label: Beach slope
attrs.tooltip:
How steeply the beach shelves into the water. Gentle gives
a wide tidal flat; steep gives a narrow strand under a
bluff.

attrs.label: Bluff sharpness
attrs.tooltip:
Steepens the cut where the terrain rises out of
the beach band — wave-cut bluffs.

attrs.label: Underwater smoothing
attrs.tooltip:
How much the ground below the waterline is smoothed. Wave
action planes off the shallows, so a seabed with the same
roughness as the hills above it reads as wrong.

attrs.label: Invert blend
attrs.tooltip:
Applies this node where the blend input is dark instead of
where it is bright.

nodes.description: Rainwater dissolves the surface into streams, strongest low down

attrs.label: Amount
attrs.tooltip:
How much rock is taken into solution. This eats out
hollows and sinkholes from within rather than cutting from
the surface, which is how limestone country gets its
pitted, karst character.

attrs.label: Rock hardness
attrs.tooltip:
Hard rock keeps the streams narrow and incised;
soft rock lets them spread and flatten the surface.

attrs.label: Low ground bias
attrs.tooltip: How much the effect concentrates at low altitude.

attrs.label: Smoothing
attrs.tooltip:
Rounds the dissolved forms. Solution features are smooth-
walled, unlike the sharp edges of mechanical erosion.

nodes.description: Erode the terrain and derive material layer masks from what the water and rock did

attrs.label: Erosion
attrs.tooltip:
Thermal weathering first drops scree below the cliffs;
the hydraulic pass then carves channels and settles silt.

attrs.label: Strength
attrs.tooltip: Scales droplet count / solver iterations.

attrs.label: Talus angle
attrs.tooltip:
The steepest slope loose material will hold before it
slides - the angle of repose. Low makes everything slump
into gentle scree cones; high lets steep faces stand.

attrs.label: Thermal iterations
attrs.tooltip:
How many passes of material shedding are run before the
layers are read off. More approaches the angle of repose
everywhere.

attrs.label: Relief (height / width)
attrs.tooltip:
How tall the terrain is compared with the tile width.
A heightmap is 0..1 over a 0..1 tile; real ground rises
a fifth of its width or less. Slopes are measured
against this, so 0.5 means 45° on the real terrain.

attrs.label: Bedrock slope
attrs.tooltip:
Slope (0 flat .. 1 vertical, 0.5 = 45°) above which
soil cannot hold and rock is exposed.

attrs.label: Grass slope limit
attrs.tooltip:
The steepest ground grass will hold on. Above this the
layer stops, which is what keeps vegetation off the cliffs
and in the hollows.

attrs.label: Sediment threshold
attrs.tooltip: How much deposited material makes a cell sand/silt.

attrs.label: Stream threshold
attrs.tooltip:
Drainage (log scale, 0..1) above which the cell is
a riverbed.

attrs.label: Snowline
attrs.tooltip:
Height above which snow lies on gentle ground.
1 = no snow.

attrs.label: Edge softness
attrs.tooltip:
How gradually one layer's mask gives way to the next. Hard
edges read as drawn on; this is what lets rock, scree,
soil and grass blend into one another.

attrs.label: Wetness spread
attrs.tooltip:
Blur radius (fraction of the map) that lets moisture
reach past the channel itself.

nodes.description: Glacial carving — broad U-shaped valleys, ridges left intact

attrs.label: Strength
attrs.tooltip:
How deeply the glacier cuts. It carves a U-shaped trough
along the drainage, which is what tells a glaciated valley
from a river one.

attrs.label: Ice line
attrs.tooltip:
Ground below this altitude is carved by ice;
peaks above it keep their sharp profile.

attrs.label: Valley width
attrs.tooltip:
How wide the trough is, as a fraction of the tile.
Glaciers cut far broader valleys than rivers of the same
catchment.

attrs.label: Rock hardness
attrs.tooltip: Hard rock resists the ice and keeps more relief.

nodes.description: Hydraulic erosion: particle droplets or shallow-water pipe model

attrs.label: Method
attrs.tooltip:
Two ways of simulating running water. Particle droplets
follow thousands of individual raindrops downhill, each
picking up and dropping sediment - fast, and good at
carving channels. Shallow water solves the whole sheet of
water at once through the pipe model, which is slower but
handles standing water and broad flow properly.

attrs.label: Particles (x1000)
attrs.tooltip:
How many droplets are released, in thousands. More is
smoother and more thoroughly carved, and costs
proportionally more.

attrs.label: Particle lifetime
attrs.tooltip:
How many steps a droplet takes before it gives up. Short
lives erode near the ridges only; long ones carry sediment
all the way to the basins.

attrs.label: Inertia
attrs.tooltip:
How much a droplet keeps its heading rather than turning
straight downhill. Low follows the terrain exactly and
gives tight, branching channels; high sweeps across
contours and gives straighter, broader valleys.

attrs.label: Carry capacity
attrs.tooltip:
How much sediment a droplet can hold, per unit of speed
and slope. This is the main dial for how deeply the
terrain is cut: a droplet erodes while it is under
capacity and deposits once it is over.

attrs.label: Erosion rate
attrs.tooltip:
How fast a droplet takes material when it has room to
carry more. High values cut sharp gullies quickly and can
punch through thin ridges.

attrs.label: Deposition rate
attrs.tooltip:
How fast a droplet drops material once it is carrying more
than it can hold. This is what builds the fans and flats
at the bottom of the slope.

attrs.label: Evaporation
attrs.tooltip:
How fast a droplet shrinks as it travels. Faster
evaporation shortens its reach and makes it drop its load
sooner, which piles sediment higher up the slope.

attrs.label: Gravity
attrs.tooltip:
How strongly slope accelerates a droplet. Higher makes
fast water on steep ground far more erosive than slow
water on flat.

attrs.label: Brush radius
attrs.tooltip:
How wide an area each droplet takes material from. 1 gives
thin, noisy scratches; wider spreads the cut and gives
smoother, more believable channels.

attrs.label: Iterations
attrs.tooltip:
How many time steps the water sheet is advanced. This is
the main cost and the main dial for how far the erosion
has progressed.

attrs.label: Rainfall
attrs.tooltip:
How much water falls per step, everywhere. More water
means more flow, deeper channels and more standing water
in the hollows.

attrs.label: Capacity Kc
attrs.tooltip:
How much sediment the flow can carry for a given speed and
slope. The single strongest control on how deeply the
terrain is cut.

attrs.label: Erosion Ks
attrs.tooltip:
How fast the bed gives up material where the flow is under
capacity.

attrs.label: Deposition Kd
attrs.tooltip:
How fast sediment settles where the flow is over capacity.
High values fill the basins quickly and flatten them.

attrs.label: Evaporation
attrs.tooltip:
How fast standing water disappears each step. Low leaves
lakes in the hollows; high dries the map between rainfalls
and concentrates the cutting in the channels.

nodes.description: The erosion look at one percent of the cost

attrs.label: Radius (px)
attrs.tooltip:
How far the smoothing reaches. This is a blur that follows
the drainage, so it softens the slopes water would have
run down while leaving the ridge lines alone.

attrs.label: Amount
attrs.tooltip:
How much of the blurred result is mixed in. Full strength
reads as a landscape long weathered; a little takes the
hard edges off fresh erosion.

attrs.label: Keep ridges
Invert blend
attrs.tooltip:
Applies this node where the blend input is dark instead of
where it is bright.

nodes.description: Trace rivers from headwaters and carve channels; outputs river + depth masks

attrs.label: Headwaters
attrs.tooltip:
Number of river source points seeded on high ground
with strong drainage; streams merge downstream.

attrs.label: River width
attrs.tooltip: How wide the channel is cut, as a fraction of the tile.

attrs.label: Carve depth
attrs.tooltip:
How deeply the channel is cut below the surrounding
ground.

attrs.label: Valley width
attrs.tooltip: Soft V-shaped valley carved around the channel.

attrs.label: Widen downstream
attrs.tooltip:
How much the channel broadens as more water joins it. 0
gives a ditch of constant width the whole way; higher
makes the headwaters narrow and the lower reaches broad,
which is what a real drainage network looks like.

attrs.label: Invert blend
attrs.tooltip:
Applies this node where the blend input is dark instead of
where it is bright.

nodes.description: Fill valleys with smooth sediment

attrs.label: Iterations
attrs.tooltip:
How many settling passes are run. More lets sediment
travel further downhill before it comes to rest.

attrs.label: Fill amount
attrs.tooltip:
How much material is deposited into the hollows. This is
the counterpart to erosion: it fills the low ground and
flattens the basins rather than cutting the high ground.

nodes.description: Fluvial erosion E=K·A^m·S^n — explicit incision or implicit solver with tectonic uplift

attrs.label: Method
attrs.tooltip:
How the incision law is stepped. The explicit scheme is
simple and fast but needs a small time step to stay
stable; the implicit one (Braun and Willett) is
unconditionally stable and lets you take large steps,
which is how you get a mature drainage network without
waiting.

attrs.label: Iterations
attrs.tooltip:
How many time steps the incision law is advanced. This is
the main cost and the main dial for how mature the
drainage network becomes.

attrs.label: Erodibility K
attrs.tooltip:
How erodible the rock is. This is the overall rate of the
whole process - harder rock, slower incision, and a
landscape that keeps its steep ground for longer.

attrs.label: Area exponent m
attrs.tooltip:
How strongly drainage area drives incision. Higher makes
the big rivers cut far faster than the small ones, which
deepens the main valleys and leaves the tributaries
hanging.

attrs.label: Slope exponent n (explicit)
Timestep (implicit)
attrs.tooltip:
The time step. Larger advances the landscape faster per
iteration; with the explicit method too large a step goes
unstable and spikes.

attrs.label: Uplift rate
attrs.tooltip:
How fast the land is pushed up while the rivers cut down.
A landscape only reaches a steady shape when the two are
in balance, and this is what stops the terrain simply
wearing flat.

attrs.label: Diffusion
attrs.tooltip:
Smooths the result at the end, which takes off the
numerical roughness the solver leaves without undoing the
drainage pattern it found.

nodes.description: Thermal weathering — talus slopes to angle of repose

attrs.label: Talus angle (legacy)
attrs.tooltip:
Relief units per texel. Used only while the angle of
repose below is 0.

attrs.label: Angle of repose
attrs.tooltip:
In degrees on the real terrain: scree settles at about
35°, dry sand at 30-34°, wet soil steeper. 0 keeps the
legacy talus value.

attrs.label: Relief (height / width)
attrs.tooltip:
How tall the terrain is against the tile width; the
angle above is measured against this.

attrs.label: Iterations
attrs.tooltip:
How many passes of material are shed. More approaches the
angle of repose everywhere and costs proportionally.

attrs.label: Transport rate
attrs.tooltip:
How much material moves per pass. Low is a slow, even
creep; high collapses the slopes quickly and can overshoot
into terracing.

attrs.label: Run to convergence
attrs.tooltip:
Stops early once a pass moves less than this, so a terrain
that has already reached its angle of repose does not keep
paying for iterations that do nothing.

nodes.description: Aeolian erosion — windward abrasion, leeward deposition (dunes)

attrs.label: Wind direction °
attrs.tooltip:
Which way the wind blows. Everything this node does is
oriented by it: material is lifted from the windward faces
and dropped in the lee.

attrs.label: Iterations
attrs.tooltip:
How many passes of transport are run. More moves material
further and settles the dunes into longer, more continuous
forms.

attrs.label: Strength
attrs.tooltip:
How much material the wind lifts per pass. High scours the
exposed ground hard and piles it deep behind obstacles.

attrs.label: Carry distance
attrs.tooltip:
How far the wind carries a grain before dropping it, as a
fraction of the tile. Short gives sharp drifts against
every obstruction; long spreads material across the whole
map.

attrs.label: Shadow angle
attrs.tooltip:
How far into the lee of a rise the wind stays too weak to
lift anything. This is what creates the sheltered pocket
where sand accumulates, and the reason dunes form downwind
of an obstacle rather than on it.

nodes.description: Write 16-bit PNG / RAW heightmap

attrs.label: File
attrs.tooltip: Where the file is written.

attrs.label: Format
attrs.tooltip:
PNG keeps 16 bits per sample, which is enough for terrain
in most cases; RAW float32 keeps the full precision and is
what another tool should read.

attrs.label: Export on every compute
attrs.tooltip:
Writes the file every time the graph recomputes.
Convenient while iterating, and a great deal of disk
traffic if left on.

nodes.description: Writes the terrain as an OBJ mesh, for another application to open

attrs.label: File
attrs.tooltip: Where the file is written.

attrs.label: Mesh resolution
attrs.tooltip:
How many vertices the exported mesh has along each side.
This is the resolution of the exported geometry, not of
the graph.

attrs.label: Height scale
attrs.tooltip:
How the terrain's heights are scaled into the mesh, so it
lands at the right proportions elsewhere.

attrs.label: Export on every compute
attrs.tooltip:
Writes the file every time the graph recomputes.
Convenient while iterating, and a great deal of disk
traffic if left on.

nodes.description: Write a point cloud or path to CSV / PLY

attrs.label: File
attrs.tooltip: Where the file is written.

attrs.label: Format
attrs.tooltip:
CSV is readable anywhere; PLY carries the points as real
geometry.

attrs.label: Height scale
attrs.tooltip:
How the stored heights are scaled on the way out, so the
cloud lands at the right size in whatever reads it.

attrs.label: Export on every compute
attrs.tooltip:
Writes the file every time the graph recomputes.
Convenient while iterating, and a great deal of disk
traffic if left on.

nodes.description: Writes a texture out as a PNG, so a material built here can be used elsewhere

attrs.label: File
attrs.tooltip: Where the file is written.

attrs.label: Export on every compute
attrs.tooltip:
Writes the file every time the graph recomputes.
Convenient while iterating, and a great deal of disk
traffic if left on.

nodes.description: Shapes planets and the infinite ground plane from a field graph

attrs.label: Strength
attrs.tooltip:
Weight of this field against the built-in layers.
They span roughly -0.5..0.5 of the relief budget, so
1.0 makes the field as strong as a full layer.

attrs.label: Update the viewport
attrs.tooltip:
Off: keep the graph but stop shaping the surfaces,
without having to disconnect it.

nodes.description: Displaces the viewport terrain on the GPU from a field graph

attrs.label: Strength
attrs.tooltip:
How far the field moves the surface, in world units
(the terrain tile is 1 unit across).

attrs.label: Update the viewport
attrs.tooltip:
Off: keep the graph but stop displacing, without having
to disconnect it.

nodes.description: Final terrain: combines height layers + material, zero edges

attrs.label: Combine layers
attrs.tooltip:
How the extra height layers are folded into the main one.
Max keeps both shapes where they overlap; add sums them
and can double the relief.

attrs.label: Layer strength
attrs.tooltip: How strongly the extra layers count.

attrs.label: Zero edges width
attrs.tooltip:
Fades terrain to zero at the borders — the final
island/tile edge treatment.

attrs.label: Edge curve
attrs.tooltip:
The profile the terrain takes as it falls to the border.
Steep leaves a cliff at the tile edge; smooth eases it
out.

attrs.label: Final height range
attrs.tooltip: The low and high the finished terrain is rescaled into.

attrs.label: Remap to range
attrs.tooltip:
Rescales the result into the range above. Off keeps the
raw values, which matters when the numbers themselves mean
something.

nodes.description: Shades the viewport terrain from a field graph, per pixel on the GPU

attrs.label: Bump strength
attrs.tooltip:
How strongly the bump field tilts the surface normal.
This is shading only — it does not move the geometry,
which is what TerrainDisplacement is for.

attrs.label: Bump sample distance
attrs.tooltip:
How far apart the bump is sampled. Too small and it is
noise; too large and it flattens.

attrs.label: Update the viewport
attrs.tooltip:
Off: keep the graph but go back to the usual shading,
without having to disconnect it.

nodes.description: Bakes a field into a heightmap so raster nodes (erosion, blur) can work on it

attrs.label: Region centre
attrs.tooltip:
The middle of the region of the field that is baked, in
field coordinates.

attrs.label: Region size
attrs.tooltip:
How much of the field's space this buffer covers.
Smaller values zoom in — the field has no resolution of
its own, so this is what decides the detail you capture.

attrs.label: Sample height
attrs.tooltip: The Y plane the field is sampled on, for 3D fields.

attrs.label: Remap to range
attrs.tooltip:
Rescales the result so its lowest point sits at the
bottom of the range below and its highest at the top.
Off keeps the raw values, which is what you want when
a node feeds arithmetic rather than a picture.

attrs.label: Output range
attrs.tooltip:
The low and high the result is rescaled into. 0..1 is
the terrain's own range; a narrower band makes this
node a gentler contribution when it is added to
another.

attrs.label: Invert
attrs.tooltip:
Turns the result upside down within its range - peaks
become hollows. Applied after the remap.

attrs.label: Gain (gamma)
attrs.tooltip:
Bends the result toward its low or high end. Below 1
lifts the middle, so more of the map sits high; above
1 pushes it down, so peaks become sparser and sharper.

attrs.label: Zero edges width
attrs.tooltip:
Fades the terrain to zero at the borders over this
fraction of the map — clean edges for islands/tiles.

nodes.description: Reads a heightmap as a field, so sculpted or eroded terrain can drive a shader

attrs.label: Region centre
attrs.tooltip: The middle of the region of the buffer that is read.

attrs.label: Region size
attrs.tooltip: How much of the buffer the region covers.

attrs.label: Value scale
attrs.tooltip: Multiplies the values read out of the buffer.

attrs.label: Repeat outside the region
attrs.tooltip:
Off: points outside the buffer clamp to its edge.
On: the buffer tiles infinitely.

nodes.description: Colour correction: hue shift, saturation, contrast, brightness, gamma, invert

attrs.label: Hue shift °
attrs.tooltip: Rotates every colour around the wheel, in degrees.

attrs.label: Saturation
attrs.tooltip: How strong the colour is. 0 leaves greyscale.

attrs.label: Contrast
attrs.tooltip: Pushes colours away from the middle, or toward it below 1.

attrs.label: Brightness
attrs.tooltip: Added to every channel.

attrs.label: Gamma
attrs.tooltip: Bends the midtones without moving black or white.

attrs.label: Invert
attrs.tooltip: Turns every colour into its opposite.

nodes.description: Builds a colour from hue, saturation, value and alpha numbers

attrs.label: Hue (when unconnected)
attrs.tooltip:
The hue used when nothing is wired to it, 0..1 around the
wheel.

attrs.label: Saturation (when unconnected)
attrs.tooltip: The saturation used when nothing is wired to it.

attrs.label: Value (when unconnected)
attrs.tooltip: The brightness used when nothing is wired to it.

attrs.label: Alpha (when unconnected)
attrs.tooltip: The alpha used when nothing is wired to it.

nodes.description: Takes a colour apart as hue, saturation and value (each 0..1)
Blends two colours — mix, add, multiply, screen, overlay, darken, lighten

attrs.label: Blend mode
attrs.tooltip: How the two colours are combined.

attrs.label: Amount (when unconnected)
attrs.tooltip:
How much of the second colour is mixed in, when nothing is
wired to the factor.

nodes.description: Turns a number into a colour through a gradient

attrs.label: Gradient
attrs.tooltip: The colour ramp the incoming number is looked up in.

attrs.label: Input range
attrs.tooltip:
The span of input values that maps across the whole
gradient. Anything outside takes the nearest end.

nodes.description: Builds a colour from red, green, blue and alpha numbers

attrs.label: Red (when unconnected)
attrs.tooltip: The value used when nothing is wired to this input.

attrs.label: Green (when unconnected)
attrs.tooltip: The value used when nothing is wired to this input.

attrs.label: Blue (when unconnected)
attrs.tooltip: The value used when nothing is wired to this input.

attrs.label: Alpha (when unconnected)
attrs.tooltip: The value used when nothing is wired to this input.

nodes.description: Takes a colour apart: luminance, red, green, blue and alpha as numbers
Builds texture coordinates from u and v numbers

attrs.label: U (when unconnected)
attrs.tooltip: The value used when nothing is wired to this input.

attrs.label: V (when unconnected)
attrs.tooltip: The value used when nothing is wired to this input.

nodes.description: Takes texture coordinates apart into u and v numbers
Any value as a colour: grey from a number, RGB from a vector, with an alpha

attrs.label: Alpha (non-colour inputs)
attrs.tooltip:
The alpha given to a value that has no colour of its own -
a number or a vector.

attrs.label: Vector is -1..1 (remap to 0..1)
attrs.tooltip:
A direction or normal spans -1..1; on it maps that range
onto 0..1 the way a normal map does.

nodes.description: Any value as a number: luminance / length, one lane, alpha, max or average

attrs.label: Read as
attrs.tooltip:
Auto is what an unconverted link does: a colour is its
luminance, a vector its length. The lane modes pick one
component; a type with fewer lanes gives its last one.

nodes.description: Any value as texture coordinates: a vector projected on a plane, RG, or n,n

attrs.label: Project a vector on
attrs.tooltip:
Which plane a vector is flattened onto to become texture
coordinates. Ground is what you want for anything lying on
the terrain; the other two are for walls and cliffs.

nodes.description: Any value as a vector: a number broadcast, RGB of a colour, UV on a plane

attrs.label: Texture coordinates lie on
attrs.tooltip:
Which plane the texture coordinates are treated as lying
on when they are read back as a vector.

nodes.description: Builds a vector from x, y and z numbers

attrs.label: X (when unconnected)
attrs.tooltip: The value used when nothing is wired to this input.

attrs.label: Y (when unconnected)
attrs.tooltip: The value used when nothing is wired to this input.

attrs.label: Z (when unconnected)
attrs.tooltip: The value used when nothing is wired to this input.

nodes.description: Takes a vector apart: x, y, z and its length as numbers
Recovers the surface normal after displacement, so later nodes see the real shape

attrs.label: Sample distance
attrs.tooltip:
How far apart the samples are taken. Too small and the
normal is noise; too large and it smooths real detail
away. Roughly one pixel of the scale you care about.

attrs.label: Strength
attrs.tooltip:
How strongly the recovered normal tilts. This node exists
so that nodes after a displacement see the surface it
actually made rather than the flat plane it started as -
which is what makes a slope-keyed material follow the
displaced rock.

attrs.label: Flip
attrs.tooltip: Turns the recovered normal the other way up.

nodes.description: Turns a value into relief: displaces along the normal, up, or any direction

attrs.label: Direction
attrs.tooltip:
Along the normal gives relief that follows the surface,
which is what you want on a curved world. Straight up is
predictable and stacks cleanly.

attrs.label: Depth is in
attrs.tooltip:
Real units keep the displacement fixed when the scene is
rescaled; relative keeps its proportion.

attrs.label: Depth
attrs.tooltip: How far the value moves the surface. Negative presses in.

attrs.label: Reference size
attrs.tooltip: The size 'relative' depth is a fraction of.

attrs.label: Smoothing
attrs.tooltip:
Softens the displacement by sampling around each point.
Costs four extra evaluations when above zero.

attrs.label: Smoothing radius
attrs.tooltip:
How far apart the surface is sampled when working out
which way it faces. Too small reads noise as shape; too
large flattens real detail.

attrs.label: Quality boost
attrs.tooltip:
Extra octaves of detail for this displacement only, beyond
the caller's budget. Use when relief needs to be finer
than the geometry carrying it.

attrs.label: Displace outwards only
attrs.tooltip:
Discards negative displacement, so the surface can only
be pushed out and never dented inward.

attrs.label: Direction X
attrs.tooltip:
The X part of the direction the surface is pushed, when a
fixed direction is chosen rather than the normal.

attrs.label: Direction Y
attrs.tooltip:
The Y part of that direction. Straight up is the usual
choice for terrain.

attrs.label: Direction Z
attrs.tooltip: The Z part of that direction.

nodes.description: Moves where another field is evaluated — warp, flow and distortion, on anything

attrs.label: Mode
attrs.tooltip:
Offset moves the evaluation point by the vector.
Replace evaluates at the vector itself, which is how you
project one space onto another.

attrs.label: Strength
attrs.tooltip:
How far the sampling point is moved. This warps where
another field is read rather than what it returns, which
is what turns a regular pattern into a flowing one.

attrs.label: Scale X
attrs.tooltip: How much of the displacement applies along X.

attrs.label: Scale Y
attrs.tooltip: How much applies along Y.

attrs.label: Scale Z
attrs.tooltip: How much applies along Z.

nodes.description: Confines one field to a region, fading into another outside it

attrs.label: Shape
attrs.tooltip: The region the inner field is confined to.

attrs.label: Centre (X,Z)
attrs.tooltip: Where that region sits, across and along.

attrs.label: Centre Y
attrs.tooltip: The height the region is centred at.

attrs.label: Size
attrs.tooltip: How large the region is.

attrs.label: Fade
attrs.tooltip:
Width of the transition, as a fraction of the size.
Zero gives a hard edge, which will show.

attrs.label: Ignore height
attrs.tooltip:
On: the region is a column, so altitude does not matter.
Off: a true sphere or box in 3D.

nodes.description: Height of this point above the reference plane
A fixed colour, to feed any colour input

attrs.label: Colour
attrs.tooltip: The colour handed to whatever this feeds.

nodes.description: A fixed number, to feed any field input

attrs.label: Value
attrs.tooltip: The number handed to whatever this feeds.

nodes.description: Direction the surface faces at this point
Compass direction the surface faces, as -1 to 1
Position of the point being evaluated — the root of most graphs
Steepness here: 1 flat, 0 vertical, -1 flat facing down
Texture coordinates for this point — the input to any mapped texture

attrs.label: Projection
attrs.tooltip:
Which way the coordinates are projected. Top down suits
ground; the other two suit walls and cliff faces, where a
top-down projection smears.

attrs.label: Scale
attrs.tooltip: How many times the texture repeats across and along.

attrs.label: Offset
attrs.tooltip:
Slides the coordinates, which moves the texture on the
surface.

attrs.label: Rotation °
attrs.tooltip: Turns the coordinates, which rotates the texture.

nodes.description: Current time in seconds — the hook for animation
Where a material belongs: by altitude, steepness and which way the ground faces

attrs.label: By altitude
attrs.tooltip: Limits the material to a band of heights.

attrs.label: Altitude band
attrs.tooltip: The band of heights it belongs to.

attrs.label: Altitude fade
attrs.tooltip:
How gradually the material gives out at the edges of the
band. Zero gives a hard line, which will look drawn on.

attrs.label: By steepness
attrs.tooltip: Limits the material to a band of steepness.

attrs.label: Slope band
attrs.tooltip:
1 is flat ground, 0 is a vertical face. So rock wants a
low band and grass a high one.

attrs.label: Steepness fade
attrs.tooltip:
How gradually it gives out at the edges of the slope band.
Zero draws a line across the hillside.

attrs.label: By facing
attrs.tooltip: Limits the material to slopes facing a particular way.

attrs.label: Facing band
attrs.tooltip:
Which compass direction the ground faces, as -1 to 1.
Snow lingers on one side of a ridge and not the other.

attrs.label: Facing fade
attrs.tooltip:
How gradually it gives out as a slope turns away from the
favoured direction.

attrs.label: Invert
attrs.tooltip: Puts the material everywhere it would not have been.

nodes.description: Shapes a value with a curve: gain, bias, step or smoothstep

attrs.label: Shape
attrs.tooltip: The curve applied to the value.

attrs.label: Amount
attrs.tooltip: How strongly the curve bends.

attrs.label: Edges
attrs.tooltip:
The two values the curve runs between, for the step and
smoothstep shapes.

nodes.description: Combines two values: add, subtract, multiply, and the rest

attrs.label: Operation
attrs.tooltip: The arithmetic applied to the two inputs.

attrs.label: A (when unconnected)
attrs.tooltip: The first value, when nothing is wired to it.

attrs.label: B (when unconnected)
attrs.tooltip: The second value, when nothing is wired to it.

nodes.description: Blends between two inputs by a factor

attrs.label: Blend (when unconnected)
attrs.tooltip:
How far between the two inputs the result sits, when
nothing is wired to the factor.

nodes.description: Rescales a value from one range into another

attrs.label: Input range
attrs.tooltip: The span of input values that is rescaled.

attrs.label: Output range
attrs.tooltip:
The span they are rescaled into. Reversing it turns the
value upside down.

attrs.label: Clamp to the output range
attrs.tooltip:
Holds the result inside the output range instead of
letting it run past the ends.

nodes.description: Trigonometry: sine, cosine, tangent and their inverses

attrs.label: Function
attrs.tooltip: The trigonometric function applied.

attrs.label: Work in degrees
attrs.tooltip:
Interpret the input (and produce the output of the
inverse functions) in degrees rather than radians.

attrs.label: Input scale
attrs.tooltip:
Multiplies the input before the function, which sets how
many cycles it goes through across the terrain.

nodes.description: Vector maths: length, dot, distance, normalize, cross, add, subtract, multiply, reflect

attrs.label: Operation
attrs.tooltip:
'out' is a number: the scalar result, or the X lane of a
vector result. 'vec' is the whole vector result; for the
scalar operations it passes A through (A - B for Distance).

nodes.description: A sward of grass - tufts, blades and bare ground - as a function, at any scale

attrs.label: Tuft size (m)
attrs.tooltip:
How far across one tuft of grass is, in metres. 0.12 is
a clump of meadow grass, 0.03 is a lawn, 1 is tussock.

Below about a centimetre on a 5 km tile the tile's own
coordinates run out of precision and the tufts go
blocky. Shrink the terrain, not the grass.

attrs.label: Blade height (m)
attrs.tooltip:
How tall the longest blades stand, in metres. Grass is
taller than it is wide, which is most of what tells it
apart from a field of small stones.

attrs.label: Sizes
attrs.tooltip:
How many halvings of the tuft size to add, so how wide
a range of sizes one sward holds - big clumps with
finer grass filling between them.

attrs.label: Amount
attrs.tooltip:
How much grass there is. Up to about three quarters it
thins the sward; past that every cell holds a tuft and
they grow into one another, so 1 closes it completely
with no ground showing through.

attrs.label: Pointedness
attrs.tooltip:
How sharply a tuft comes to a point. This is the one
control that most decides whether the field reads as
grass or as gravel: 0 gives domes, which is what a
stone is, and no amount of blade detail rescues that.

attrs.label: Blade relief
attrs.tooltip:
How strongly the individual blades show against the
tuft they belong to. 0 is a smooth mound.

attrs.label: Blade count
attrs.tooltip: 0 a few broad blades, 1 many fine ones.

attrs.label: Size variation
attrs.tooltip:
0: every tuft the same size. 1: many small tufts and a
few large, which is what a real sward has.

attrs.label: Shape variation
attrs.tooltip:
How much tufts differ from one another. 0 shapes every
tuft in the field alike, which is the look of a
texture; 1 puts fine soft grass and coarse spiky
clumps side by side.

attrs.label: Height variation
attrs.tooltip:
How much tufts differ in height from one another,
about the average. The average is unchanged
whatever this is set to.

attrs.label: Size mix
attrs.tooltip:
Which sizes the field is actually made of, across the
octaves it has. Below zero leans toward the large and
the small become an accent; above zero the small take
over and the large are the accent. 0 gives every size
the same share, which is what it always did.

attrs.label: Wind
attrs.tooltip:
How far the blades lean. The whole field leans one
way, which is the strongest single cue that what you
are looking at is grass and not small stones - those
each lean whichever way they fell.

attrs.label: Wind direction
attrs.tooltip: Which way the wind is blowing across the ground.

attrs.label: Tall blades bend more
attrs.tooltip:
How much further the tall blades lean than the short
ones. They do, so this is 0.5 rather than 0.

attrs.label: Cluster / repel
attrs.tooltip:
Above zero the tufts gather into patches and are
pulled together inside one; below zero they stand off
from one another. The count is unchanged either way.

attrs.label: Patch size (m)
attrs.tooltip: How far across one patch of tufts is, in metres.

attrs.label: Bare ground
attrs.tooltip:
How much ground is bare of grass altogether. Grass is
not a carpet - it gives out where it is trodden, dry
or shaded - and a sward that only ever thins a little
reads as one.

attrs.label: Bare patch size (m)
attrs.tooltip: How far across a bare patch is, in metres.

attrs.label: Terrain size (m)
attrs.tooltip:
The tile's width; the studio keeps this in step with
the project so the sizes above mean metres.

nodes.description: 3D coherent noise — the basis of procedural terrain and texture

attrs.label: Type
attrs.tooltip:
The shape the octaves take - rolling ground, sharp ridges
or rounded billows.

attrs.label: Feature scale
attrs.tooltip:
How many features fit across a unit of space.
Low values give continents, high values give gravel.

attrs.label: Octaves
attrs.tooltip:
Levels of detail. Capped by the caller's level-of-detail
budget, so distant points cost less automatically.

attrs.label: Amplitude
attrs.tooltip: How far the noise swings.

attrs.label: Offset
attrs.tooltip:
Added to the result, which raises or lowers the whole
field.

nodes.description: Analytic shapes - waves, bands, bumps, cones and steps, as a function

attrs.label: Shape
attrs.tooltip: The analytic shape produced.

attrs.label: Center
attrs.tooltip: Where the shape is centred.

attrs.label: Direction
attrs.tooltip:
Which way the waves run, the band lies, or the step
faces, in degrees on the ground plane.

attrs.label: Frequency
attrs.tooltip: Wave repetitions per unit of ground. Waves only.

attrs.label: Width
attrs.tooltip: Radius of the bump or cone; thickness of the band.

attrs.label: Phase
attrs.tooltip: Slides a wave along, as a fraction of one cycle.

attrs.label: Amplitude
attrs.tooltip: How far the result swings.

attrs.label: Offset
attrs.tooltip: Added to the result.

nodes.description: A field of stones - boulders, cobbles and gravel - as a function, at any scale

attrs.label: Stone size (m)
attrs.tooltip:
The biggest stone's width across, in metres, and it is
really metres: 0.12 is a cobble, 0.02 is grit, 3 is a
boulder. Every size below it comes from the octaves,
each half as wide and four times as many, so one field
holds boulders, cobbles and grit at once.

Below about a centimetre across on a 5 km tile the
tile's own coordinates run out of precision and the
outlines go blocky. Shrink the terrain, not the stone.

attrs.label: Sizes
attrs.tooltip:
How many halvings of the stone size to add, so how wide
a range of sizes one field holds. 1 is a single size;
6 spans thirty-two to one, boulders down to grit.
Distance takes octaves away again, so this is a
ceiling, not a cost.

attrs.label: Amount
attrs.tooltip:
How much stone there is. Up to about three quarters it
thins the field; past that every cell holds a stone and
they grow into one another, so 1 paves the ground end
to end with no bare earth left between.

attrs.label: Tallness
attrs.tooltip: A stone's height as a fraction of its radius.

attrs.label: Height variation
attrs.tooltip:
How much stones differ in height from one another,
about the average. The average is unchanged
whatever this is, so widening the spread does not
quietly raise or lower the whole field.

attrs.label: Size mix
attrs.tooltip:
Which sizes the field is actually made of, across the
octaves it has. Below zero leans toward the large and
the small become an accent; above zero the small take
over and the large are the accent. 0 gives every size
the same share, which is what it always did.

attrs.label: Size variation
attrs.tooltip:
0: every stone the same size. 1: the power-law
spectrum a scree slope has - many small, a few large.

attrs.label: Shape variation
attrs.tooltip:
How much stones differ from one another. 0 breaks,
flattens and pits every stone in the field to exactly
the same degree, which is the look of a texture; 1 puts
rounded cobbles and shattered blocks side by side, the
way real scree does.

attrs.label: Flatten
attrs.tooltip:
Raises the top into a plateau while keeping the
footprint: 0 boulders, 1 slabs.

attrs.label: Settled into the ground
attrs.tooltip:
How deep a stone sits. Buried stones show only their
tops, and the ground cuts their outline instead of
meeting them tangentially.

attrs.label: Elongation
attrs.tooltip:
How much longer a stone may be one way than the other,
turned as it fell. Round in plan is the tell of a
procedural field.

attrs.label: Outline roughness
attrs.tooltip: How far the outline departs from an ellipse.

attrs.label: Broken faces
attrs.tooltip:
Cuts flat faces into each stone. 0 leaves rounded
pebbles; high values give the angular, broken look of
quarried or frost-shattered rock.

attrs.label: Surface relief
attrs.tooltip:
How far a stone's own surface departs from a smooth
shell. 0 is polished.

attrs.label: Lean
attrs.tooltip:
Moves each stone's high point off centre, so it has a
downhill side rather than being a dome.

attrs.label: Cluster / repel
attrs.tooltip:
Stones are not spread evenly. Above zero they collect
in drifts with bare ground between, and are pulled
together inside a drift until they lie shoulder to
shoulder - 1 heaps them hard. Below zero they push
apart instead and stand off from one another, the way
frost heave sorts a boulder field. The count is
unchanged either way: this rearranges a field, it does
not thin it.

attrs.label: Drift size (m)
attrs.tooltip: How far across one clump of stones is, in metres.

attrs.label: Terrain size (m)
attrs.tooltip:
The tile's width; the studio keeps this in step with
the project so the size above means metres.

nodes.description: Cellular (Worley) noise - cracks, plates, scree and crater fields

attrs.label: Cell size
attrs.tooltip:
How many cells fit across a unit of space.
Low values give continent-sized plates, high values
give gravel.

attrs.label: Jitter
attrs.tooltip:
How far each cell's point may wander from its centre.
0 is a perfect grid; 1 is fully irregular.

attrs.label: Octaves
attrs.tooltip:
Stacks the cells at rising frequency and falling
weight, the way fBm stacks noise: continents of
plates with gravel in the cracks. 1 is the plain
pattern.

attrs.label: Cell shape
attrs.tooltip:
The distance the cells are measured with, which is
what decides their silhouette.

attrs.label: Pattern
attrs.tooltip:
F1 is zero at each cell's own point and rises outward: cell
centres become pits and the seams between them become ridges.
Crater fields, dimpled rock.

F2 is the same one cell further out - rounder, smoother swells.

F2 - F1 is zero exactly on the seam between two cells and
highest at the centre: domes with sharp creases between them.
Invert it and the seams become the cracks.

Flat cell value gives each cell one random height - plates,
terraces, tectonic blocks.

attrs.label: Amplitude
attrs.tooltip: How far the cellular pattern swings.

attrs.label: Offset
attrs.tooltip: Added to the result.

attrs.label: Invert
attrs.tooltip: Turns pits into domes, and walls into channels.

nodes.description: Clamp with optional smooth shoulders

attrs.label: Clamp range
attrs.tooltip:
Everything below the low value is lifted to it and
everything above the high value pushed down to it -
flat floors and flat tops, with the middle
untouched.

attrs.label: Shoulder softness
attrs.tooltip:
Rounds the corner where the terrain meets the clamp
instead of cutting it flat. 0 leaves a hard crease
that catches the light as a line.

nodes.description: Convolution by a preset or typed kernel

attrs.label: Kernel
attrs.tooltip:
A small matrix swept over the map. Sharpen boosts
local contrast; the edge and Sobel kernels find
boundaries and make good masks rather than terrain;
Emboss lights it from one side. Custom takes your
own numbers below.

attrs.label: Custom (row-major)
attrs.tooltip: 9 or 25 numbers, row-major 3x3 or 5x5, any whitespace.

attrs.label: Strength
attrs.tooltip: Scales the kernel's result before it is used.

attrs.label: Add to input
attrs.tooltip:
On, the result is added on top of the original
terrain instead of replacing it - which is how an
edge kernel becomes extra relief along the breaks
rather than a picture of them.

attrs.label: Invert blend
attrs.tooltip:
Applies this node where the blend input is dark instead of
where it is bright.

nodes.description: Slope-targeted rocky detail; flats stay clean

attrs.label: Detail scale
attrs.tooltip:
How fine the added crag detail is, in repeats across
the tile. High values give the broken texture of
shattered rock; low ones give lumps.

attrs.label: Strength
attrs.tooltip:
How far the crags stand off the surface. This is
surface roughness, not landform - a little goes a
long way.

attrs.label: Slope threshold
attrs.tooltip:
How steep ground must be before crags appear on it.
Bare broken rock belongs on the steeps; flat ground
collects soil and stays smooth.

attrs.label: Threshold softness
attrs.tooltip:
How gradually the crags fade in as the slope
steepens, so the treated ground does not end on a
line.

attrs.label: Octaves
attrs.tooltip: How many sizes of crag are layered together.

nodes.description: Remaps elevations through a drawn curve - the gradient's brightness is the transfer function

attrs.label: Curve
attrs.tooltip:
The transfer curve, read as brightness: the horizontal
axis is the height coming in, the gradient's brightness at
that point is the height going out. A straight ramp
changes nothing; bending it up raises the midlands, an S
makes the flats flatter and the steeps steeper.

attrs.label: Strength
attrs.tooltip:
How much of the curved result replaces the original. Part-
way is a gentler version of the same shaping.

attrs.label: Remap to range
attrs.tooltip:
Rescales the result so its lowest point sits at the
bottom of the range below and its highest at the top.
Off keeps the raw values, which is what you want when
a node feeds arithmetic rather than a picture.

attrs.label: Output range
attrs.tooltip:
The low and high the result is rescaled into. 0..1 is
the terrain's own range; a narrower band makes this
node a gentler contribution when it is added to
another.

attrs.label: Invert
attrs.tooltip:
Turns the result upside down within its range - peaks
become hollows. Applied after the remap.

attrs.label: Gain (gamma)
attrs.tooltip:
Bends the result toward its low or high end. Below 1
lifts the middle, so more of the map sits high; above
1 pushes it down, so peaks become sparser and sharper.

attrs.label: Zero edges width
attrs.tooltip:
Fades the terrain to zero at the borders over this
fraction of the map — clean edges for islands/tiles.

nodes.description: Per-band detail gains, like an audio EQ

attrs.label: Fine (1-4 px)
attrs.tooltip:
The grain of the surface. Turning it down calms a
noisy terrain without softening its shape; turning
it up sharpens the texture without adding relief.

attrs.label: Medium (4-16 px)
attrs.tooltip:
Gullies and small outcrops - the scale that carries
most of a landscape's character.

attrs.label: Coarse (16-64 px)
attrs.tooltip: Ridges and valleys: the landforms themselves.

attrs.label: Base (blur 64 px+)
attrs.tooltip:
The overall lie of the land under everything else.
Turning this down flattens the map without losing
any of its detail - all four bands together are the
original, so 1 everywhere changes nothing.

attrs.label: Invert blend
attrs.tooltip:
Applies this node where the blend input is dark instead of
where it is bright.

nodes.description: Subtract the best-fit plane

attrs.label: Amount
attrs.tooltip:
How much of the overall tilt is removed. An imported
heightfield often leans as a whole; taking the plane
out levels it without touching the relief on top.

attrs.label: Invert blend
attrs.tooltip:
Applies this node where the blend input is dark instead of
where it is bright.

nodes.description: Streak the surface along a direction

attrs.label: Direction °
attrs.tooltip:
Which way the streaks run. Along the prevailing wind
this reads as scouring; down the slope, as material
having run.

attrs.label: Length
attrs.tooltip:
How far the smearing reaches, as a fraction of the
tile.

attrs.label: Both directions
attrs.tooltip:
On, it smears symmetrically and the surface stays
put. Off, it drags one way only, so features shift
downstream as well as blurring - which is what makes
it look like flow rather than blur.

attrs.label: Invert blend
attrs.tooltip:
Applies this node where the blend input is dark instead of
where it is bright.

nodes.description: Spreads elevations across the full range - contrast back after a long chain

attrs.label: Strength
attrs.tooltip:
1 is full equalisation; lower blends back toward the
original distribution.

attrs.label: Remap to range
attrs.tooltip:
Rescales the result so its lowest point sits at the
bottom of the range below and its highest at the top.
Off keeps the raw values, which is what you want when
a node feeds arithmetic rather than a picture.

attrs.label: Output range
attrs.tooltip:
The low and high the result is rescaled into. 0..1 is
the terrain's own range; a narrower band makes this
node a gentler contribution when it is added to
another.

attrs.label: Invert
attrs.tooltip:
Turns the result upside down within its range - peaks
become hollows. Applied after the remap.

attrs.label: Gain (gamma)
attrs.tooltip:
Bends the result toward its low or high end. Below 1
lifts the middle, so more of the map sits high; above
1 pushes it down, so peaks become sparser and sharper.

attrs.label: Zero edges width
attrs.tooltip:
Fades the terrain to zero at the borders over this
fraction of the map — clean edges for islands/tiles.

nodes.description: Morphological dilate / erode

attrs.label: Radius
attrs.tooltip:
How far the high ground grows outward, as a fraction
of the tile. On a mask this fattens or thins the
selected region; on terrain it broadens ridges or
widens valleys.

attrs.label: Shrink (erode)
attrs.tooltip:
Runs it the other way: the low ground grows instead,
eating into the high. Expand then shrink at the same
radius closes small gaps and leaves the rest alone.

nodes.description: Fold values around midline — creates ridged detail

attrs.label: Iterations
attrs.tooltip:
How many times the heights are reflected about the
middle. Each fold turns every valley into a ridge,
so one pass makes smooth noise ridged and several
make an intricate crumpled surface. This is where
ridged noise comes from, applied after the fact.

nodes.description: Bends the heights toward the low or the high end without moving either

attrs.label: Gamma
attrs.tooltip:
Bends the heights toward the low or the high end
without moving either. Below 1 lifts the middle, so
more of the map sits high and the lowland shrinks;
above 1 pushes it down, so peaks become sparse and
the valleys broad.

nodes.description: Edge-preserving smoothing (painterly flats)

attrs.label: Radius (px)
attrs.tooltip:
How far it looks for a flat neighbourhood to average
instead. Unlike a blur this keeps the edges: it
flattens the ground between features while leaving
the breaks between them sharp.

attrs.label: Mix
Invert blend
attrs.tooltip:
Applies this node where the blend input is dark instead of
where it is bright.

nodes.description: Mode-seeking smoothing (flattens toward plateaus)

attrs.label: Radius (px)
attrs.tooltip:
How far across the map each point looks for company.
Larger merges more ground into each plateau.

attrs.label: Value tolerance
attrs.tooltip:
How close in height two points must be to count as
the same surface. This is what keeps a cliff a cliff
while the ground either side of it flattens: only
similar heights are averaged together.

attrs.label: Iterations
attrs.tooltip:
How many times the search is repeated. Each pass
moves points further toward the nearest flat, so
more of them converge into fewer, cleaner terraces.

attrs.label: Invert blend
attrs.tooltip:
Applies this node where the blend input is dark instead of
where it is bright.

nodes.description: Removes single-cell spikes and pits without softening edges

attrs.label: Radius
attrs.tooltip:
1 looks at 3x3 cells, 2 at 5x5, 3 at 7x7. Larger wipes
bigger artifacts and more real detail with them.

attrs.label: Passes
attrs.tooltip:
Applying it again flattens what one pass left; a few
passes approach a stable, blocky simplification.

attrs.label: Remap to range
attrs.tooltip:
Rescales the result so its lowest point sits at the
bottom of the range below and its highest at the top.
Off keeps the raw values, which is what you want when
a node feeds arithmetic rather than a picture.

attrs.label: Output range
attrs.tooltip:
The low and high the result is rescaled into. 0..1 is
the terrain's own range; a narrower band makes this
node a gentler contribution when it is added to
another.

attrs.label: Invert
attrs.tooltip:
Turns the result upside down within its range - peaks
become hollows. Applied after the remap.

attrs.label: Gain (gamma)
attrs.tooltip:
Bends the result toward its low or high end. Below 1
lifts the middle, so more of the map sits high; above
1 pushes it down, so peaks become sparser and sharper.

attrs.label: Zero edges width
attrs.tooltip:
Fades the terrain to zero at the borders over this
fraction of the map — clean edges for islands/tiles.

nodes.description: Dilate, erode and their compositions

attrs.label: Operation
attrs.tooltip:
Dilate grows the bright regions, erode shrinks them. Open
is erode then dilate - it removes specks and leaves
everything else the same size. Close is the reverse and
fills small holes. The two are how you clean up a mask
without blurring it.

attrs.label: Radius (px)
attrs.tooltip:
How far the operation reaches. On a mask this is the
size of the gap it can close or the speck it can
remove.

attrs.label: Element
attrs.tooltip:
The neighbourhood the operation uses. A square is fastest
but leaves corners on round features; the octagon is
closer to a circle and does not.

attrs.label: Invert blend
attrs.tooltip:
Applies this node where the blend input is dark instead of
where it is bright.

nodes.description: Flatten tops above a level

attrs.label: Level
attrs.tooltip:
The height everything above is flattened to. This is
how a mesa or a tableland is made from a hill: the
summit is cut off level and the flanks keep their
shape.

attrs.label: Softness

nodes.description: Terragen-style multi-scale fractal displacement

attrs.label: Noise flavour
attrs.tooltip:
Which noise the displacement is built from. Each has a
different character at the same settings - one gives
rolling forms, another sharp ridges, another cellular
blocks.

attrs.label: Lead-in scale
attrs.tooltip:
Largest visible variation (fraction of terrain width).
Octaves between lead-in and feature scale ramp in
with reduced amplitude.

attrs.label: Feature scale
attrs.tooltip: Scale of the dominant, full-amplitude features.

attrs.label: Smallest scale
attrs.tooltip: Detail cutoff — nothing finer than this is added.

attrs.label: Displacement amplitude
attrs.tooltip:
How far the pattern displaces the surface, in heightmap
units. This is the strength of the whole effect.

attrs.label: Displacement offset
attrs.tooltip:
Shifts displacement: positive raises plinths,
negative sinks features.

attrs.label: Roughness
attrs.tooltip:
Per-octave gain multiplier; below 1 smooths high
frequencies, above 1 exaggerates them.

attrs.label: Spike limit
attrs.tooltip:
Damps octave contributions on already-steep ground
to prevent needle spikes.

attrs.label: Displace along normal
attrs.tooltip:
Scales displacement with slope so cliffs bulge
outward like real overhung rock (approximated).

attrs.label: Apply on slopes
attrs.tooltip:
Restrict displacement to this normalized slope band
(e.g. 0.4..1 = only on steep faces).

attrs.label: Slope softness
attrs.tooltip:
How gradually the effect fades in as the slope steepens,
so treated ground does not end on a visible line.

nodes.description: Rescales the whole map into a new range, keeping its shape exactly

attrs.label: Target range
attrs.tooltip:
Rescales the whole map so its lowest point lands on
the first value and its highest on the second.
Nothing is clipped - the shape is unchanged, only
its range. Reversing the two turns the terrain
upside down.

attrs.label: Invert blend
attrs.tooltip:
Applies this node where the blend input is dark instead of
where it is bright.

nodes.description: Softens the surface: takes the noise off, and at a large radius the shape too

attrs.label: Radius
attrs.tooltip:
How far the blur reaches, as a fraction of the tile.
Small values take the noise off a surface without
touching its shape; large ones dissolve the shape
as well.

nodes.description: Fill hollows up to the smoothed surface

attrs.label: Radius (px)
attrs.tooltip:
How large a hollow counts as one worth filling.
Anything narrower than this is levelled; anything
broader is left as terrain.

attrs.label: Direction
attrs.tooltip:
Fill up raises hollows to the smoothed surface -
sediment settling into dips. Shave down cuts the
bumps off instead, which is weathering rather than
deposition. The second output reports how much was
moved, which makes a good sediment mask.

attrs.label: Amount
attrs.tooltip:
How much of the way to the smoothed surface it
goes. Part-way leaves the hollow visible but
softened.

attrs.label: Invert blend
attrs.tooltip:
Applies this node where the blend input is dark instead of
where it is bright.

nodes.description: Snow cover: snowline, settle-thaw, slip-off; outputs depth mask

attrs.label: Snow amount
attrs.tooltip:
How thick the snow lies, in heightmap units. It is added
on top of the terrain, so this also softens whatever it
covers.

attrs.label: Snowline
attrs.tooltip:
The height above which snow settles, as a fraction of the
terrain's range. Below it the ground stays bare.

attrs.label: Snowline falloff
attrs.tooltip:
How gradually the snowline is crossed. A hard line looks
painted on; real snow thins out over a band, and thins
faster on the sunnier side.

attrs.label: Slip-off slope
attrs.tooltip: Snow cannot cling to slopes steeper than this.

attrs.label: Settle-thaw iterations
attrs.tooltip:
Lets snow slide into hollows and compact —
smooth, wind-packed accumulation.

attrs.label: Melt (low areas)
attrs.tooltip:
How much snow disappears from the low, sheltered ground -
the hollows where it goes first. 0 leaves an even blanket
above the snowline.

attrs.label: Invert blend
attrs.tooltip:
Applies this node where the blend input is dark instead of
where it is bright.

nodes.description: Tilted rock strata exposed on cliff faces

attrs.label: Strength
attrs.tooltip:
How strongly the bedding shows. The beds are cut
into the existing surface rather than laid over it,
so this is how much of the original slope survives.

attrs.label: Layer count
attrs.tooltip:
How many beds are stacked through the height range.
Few gives the broad benches of a canyon wall; many
gives fine banding.

attrs.label: Tilt
attrs.tooltip:
Strata are tilted planes, not horizontal bands —
the single most important realism control.

attrs.label: Tilt direction °
attrs.tooltip:
Which way the beds dip. Sedimentary rock is rarely level,
and the direction it leans is the single strongest clue to
a landscape's geological history.

attrs.label: Warp
attrs.tooltip:
How much the beds are bent out of true. Real strata are
folded by the same forces that raised them; perfectly flat
bedding reads as printed on.

attrs.label: Substrata
attrs.tooltip: Finer secondary layering nested inside each stratum.

attrs.label: Only on slopes above
attrs.tooltip:
How steep ground must be before the strata show. Bedding
is exposed where rock is bare and cut into; gentle ground
carries soil that hides it.

attrs.label: Slope softness
attrs.tooltip:
How gradually the strata fade in as the slope steepens, so
the bedded ground does not end on a visible line.

nodes.description: Stratified terraces: uneven layers, warped edges, altitude band

attrs.label: Levels
attrs.tooltip:
How many steps the height range is cut into. Few
gives the broad benches of a canyon wall; many gives
fine bedding, and past a point they are finer than
the terrain can show.

attrs.label: Edge sharpness
Cliff bias
attrs.tooltip:
Skews each step: negative = wide flats with sharp
cliffs above; positive = sharp base, sloped tops.

attrs.label: Strength
attrs.tooltip:
How much of the terraced result replaces the
original. Below 1 leaves the underlying slope
showing through, which is usually more convincing
than a fully stepped hillside.

attrs.label: Level thickness jitter
attrs.tooltip:
Randomizes each layer's thickness — natural geological
strata are never evenly spaced.

attrs.label: Edge warp
attrs.tooltip:
Warps terrace edges with noise so contour lines
wander instead of following exact heights.

attrs.label: Edge warp scale
attrs.tooltip:
How fine the wander in the terrace edges is. Low
makes each contour meander in broad curves; high
gives a ragged, crumbling edge.

attrs.label: Altitude band
attrs.tooltip:
Only terrace heights inside this normalized band;
terrain outside is left untouched.

attrs.label: Band softness
attrs.tooltip:
How gradually the terracing fades in at the edges of
the altitude band, so the treated ground does not
end on a visible line.

nodes.description: A sub-graph collapsed into one node — group, name and reuse

attrs.label: Inner graph
attrs.tooltip:
The encapsulated graph, stored with the project.
Edit it by opening the MetaNode, not by hand.

attrs.label: Published parameters
attrs.tooltip: Which inner parameters are exposed on this node.

attrs.label: Note
attrs.tooltip:
What this MetaNode is for — it becomes the tooltip when
the node is reused from the library.

nodes.description: Floods closed basins to their outlet - filled terrain for flow routing, plus lake depth and mask

attrs.label: Drainage slope
attrs.tooltip:
A hair of tilt across each filled flat so water still
crosses it toward the outlet. Leave at 0 for true level
lakes; raise it slightly when the filled surface feeds
flow accumulation or erosion.

attrs.label: Ignore puddles below
attrs.tooltip:
Depth and mask ignore anything shallower than this, so
a thousand pinprick hollows do not read as lakes. The
filled terrain is unaffected.

attrs.label: Normalise depth
attrs.tooltip:
Scales depth to 0..1 so it can drive a mask or a blend
directly. Off leaves it in terrain units.

attrs.label: Invert blend
attrs.tooltip:
Applies this node where the blend input is dark instead of
where it is bright.

nodes.description: Standing water at a set level

attrs.label: Water level
attrs.tooltip:
The height the water stands at, as a fraction of the
terrain's own range.

attrs.label: Fill
attrs.tooltip:
Everywhere below fills every hollow at once, whether or
not water could reach it. Connected to the edge floods
only what the sea can actually get into, so a walled basin
stays dry. From source points floods outward from the
points you supply.

attrs.label: Normalize depth
attrs.tooltip:
Scales the depth output to 0..1 so it can drive a mask
directly. Off leaves it in terrain units.

attrs.label: Invert blend
attrs.tooltip:
Applies this node where the blend input is dark instead of
where it is bright.

nodes.description: A body of water at a place: centre, max radius and water level, with a wandering shore, a carved bed and a beach mask

attrs.label: Water level
attrs.tooltip:
The height of the water surface, as a fraction of the
terrain's own range. Terragen states this as a height
above the planet; here it follows the terrain so a
lake stays put when the relief is re-scaled.

attrs.label: Centre
attrs.tooltip: Where the lake sits on the tile.

attrs.label: Max radius (m)
attrs.tooltip:
The furthest the water can reach from the centre, in
metres. The wandering rim moves inside this, never
past it - which is exactly what Terragen's Max radius
means.

attrs.label: Stretch
attrs.tooltip:
1 is round, which is the only shape Terragen's Lake
can be. Higher stretches it one way, so a lake can
lie along a valley.

attrs.label: Rotation
attrs.tooltip:
Turns the lake's outline, which matters once Stretch has
pulled it away from round.

attrs.label: Outline
attrs.tooltip:
From mask takes the outline from the mask input, so a
lake can be traced from a real one.

attrs.label: Shore wander
attrs.tooltip:
How far the waterline departs from the perfect curve,
as a fraction of the radius. This is what makes bays
and spits; 0 gives the drawing-board circle.

attrs.label: Shore detail
attrs.tooltip: How many bays and headlands around the shore.

attrs.label: Shore roughness
attrs.tooltip: How much finer detail rides on the large bays.

attrs.label: Shore width
attrs.tooltip:
How far in from the rim the water shallows, as a
fraction of the lake's radius. This is the band the
'shore' output marks.

attrs.label: Shore gradient
attrs.tooltip:
The profile from the middle out to the shore. Below 1
the water stays deep and shallows abruptly - a tarn
in a rock basin. Above 1 it shallows from far out -
a wide beach.

attrs.label: Follow the ground
attrs.tooltip:
On, the lake only fills where the ground is already
below the water level, so it settles into the valley
it is in. Off, it is a flat disc that ignores the
terrain, which is what Terragen's Lake object is.

attrs.label: Carve the bed
attrs.tooltip:
Pulls the ground under the lake down below the water,
deepest in the middle. 0 leaves the terrain alone and
the water may be a film over it.

attrs.label: Bank the shore
attrs.tooltip:
Levels the ground just outside the waterline toward
the water, so the lake meets a shore rather than a
wall. This is the thing that reads as a lake.

attrs.label: Terrain size (m)
attrs.tooltip:
The tile's width; the studio keeps this in step with
the project so the radius above means metres.

attrs.label: Scene object
attrs.tooltip:
Name of the scene light this node drives. Created when missing;

attrs.label: Enabled
attrs.tooltip: Turns the light off without removing it.

attrs.label: Type

A point light throws in every direction; a spot throws in

attrs.label: Colour

attrs.label: Intensity

attrs.label: Cone angle °
