nodes.description: Compare two inputs into a mask

attrs.label: Operation
attrs.tooltip: The comparison made at every point.

attrs.label: Tolerance
attrs.tooltip:
How close two values must be to count as equal, since
exact equality between floats almost never happens.

attrs.label: Softness
attrs.tooltip:
How gradually the result crosses from false to true, so
the mask has an edge rather than a step.

nodes.description: Loop: apply an operation N times

attrs.label: Operation
attrs.tooltip: What is done on each repeat.

attrs.label: Loop count
attrs.tooltip: How many times it is repeated.

attrs.label: Strength per pass
attrs.tooltip: How much each repeat contributes.

nodes.description: Select one of four inputs by index or selector map

attrs.label: Index
attrs.tooltip:
Which input is passed through. Everything else is ignored,
which is how you switch between variants of a graph
without rewiring it.

attrs.label: Blend by selector map
attrs.tooltip:
When on, the selector map (0..1) cross-fades
between the connected inputs instead of the index.

nodes.description: Route input A or B to output

attrs.label: Use input B
attrs.tooltip:
Passes the second input instead of the first. A plain
either-or, for turning part of a graph on and off.

nodes.description: Binary/soft threshold to a mask

attrs.label: Level
attrs.tooltip: The value the input is cut at.

attrs.label: Softness
attrs.tooltip:
How gradually it crosses from 0 to 1. Zero gives a hard
edge, which on terrain reads as drawn on.

attrs.label: Invert
attrs.tooltip: Selects below the level instead of above it.

nodes.description: Pass-through / organization pin
Drop small connected blobs

attrs.label: Threshold
attrs.tooltip: The value above which a point counts as part of a patch.

attrs.label: Min area (fraction)
attrs.tooltip:
Patches smaller than this are removed. This is how you
clear speckle out of a mask without blurring the edges of
what is left.

attrs.label: Invert
attrs.tooltip:
Removes the large patches and keeps the small ones
instead.

nodes.description: Distance to a shape - shoreline gradients, wetness falloffs, anything that happens near something

attrs.label: Shape threshold
attrs.tooltip:
Where the input counts as being the shape. Feed a mask
and leave it at 0.5; feed a heightmap and this becomes
the altitude the distance is measured from.

attrs.label: Measure from the outside
attrs.tooltip:
Swap what counts as the shape: distance from dry land
instead of distance from the water.

attrs.label: Output
attrs.tooltip:
Fade: 1 at the shape, falling to 0 at the reach - a
ready-made falloff mask.
Distance: 0 at the shape, 1 at the reach.
Signed: 0.5 on the edge, below inside, above outside.

attrs.label: Reach
attrs.tooltip:
How far the field extends, as a fraction of the tile.
Everything further than this saturates.

attrs.label: Remap to range
attrs.tooltip:
Rescales the result so its lowest point sits at the
bottom of the range below and its highest at the top.
Off keeps the raw values, which is what you want when
a node feeds arithmetic rather than a picture.

attrs.label: Output range
attrs.tooltip:
The low and high the result is rescaled into. 0..1 is
the terrain's own range; a narrower band makes this
node a gentler contribution when it is added to
another.

attrs.label: Invert
attrs.tooltip:
Turns the result upside down within its range - peaks
become hollows. Applied after the remap.

attrs.label: Gain (gamma)
attrs.tooltip:
Bends the result toward its low or high end. Below 1
lifts the middle, so more of the map sits high; above
1 pushes it down, so peaks become sparser and sharper.

attrs.label: Zero edges width
attrs.tooltip:
Fades the terrain to zero at the borders over this
fraction of the map — clean edges for islands/tiles.

nodes.description: Cluster the terrain into zones

attrs.label: Clusters
attrs.tooltip:
How many regions the terrain is grouped into. Each point
joins the group whose character it most resembles, so this
is how many distinct kinds of ground you are claiming
exist.

attrs.label: Slope weight
attrs.tooltip:
How much steepness counts against height when deciding
which group a point belongs to. At 0 the grouping is
purely by altitude.

nodes.description: Paint a mask in the viewport

attrs.label: Painted mask
attrs.tooltip:
Select this node and paint in the viewport with the
Terrain Editor brushes. Raise paints in, invert (or
the eraser) paints out.

attrs.label: Soften
attrs.tooltip:
Blurs the painted mask, so a stroke's edge is a gradient
rather than the hard rim of the brush.

nodes.description: Selects the ground that lies within a band of heights - the basis of a snow line or a shore

attrs.label: Edge softness
attrs.tooltip:
How gradually the selection gives out at its edges.
Near zero gives a hard cut, which reads as drawn on; a
soft edge is what lets one material give way to
another.

attrs.label: Invert
attrs.tooltip:
Selects everything this node did not - the ground it
rejected becomes the mask.

attrs.label: Altitude band
attrs.tooltip:
The band of heights that is selected. Everything inside is
chosen, everything outside rejected, with the edge
softness above deciding how abruptly.

nodes.description: Selects ground by the compass direction it faces - the shaded north sides that hold snow, the south sides that bake dry

attrs.label: Edge softness
attrs.tooltip:
How gradually the selection gives out at its edges.
Near zero gives a hard cut, which reads as drawn on; a
soft edge is what lets one material give way to
another.

attrs.label: Invert
attrs.tooltip:
Selects everything this node did not - the ground it
rejected becomes the mask.

attrs.label: Facing
attrs.tooltip:
The compass direction the selected slopes look
towards, in degrees: 0 north, 90 east, 180 south,
270 west. This is the control nothing else in the
mask set can stand in for - altitude and steepness
cannot tell one side of a peak from the other.

attrs.label: Spread
attrs.tooltip:
How wide an arc counts as facing that way, in
degrees either side. Narrow picks one face of a
ridge; 180 selects everything and is only useful
with the flatness cut below.

attrs.label: Ignore flatter than
attrs.tooltip:
Flat ground faces nowhere in particular, and asking
it which way it points returns noise. Ground gentler
than this is dropped from the selection, which is
what keeps a valley floor from speckling.

attrs.label: Feature scale
attrs.tooltip:
How large a feature has to be to count as facing
somewhere. Small scales read every pebble and give a
speckled mask; large ones read whole hillsides, which
is what you want when the question is which side of
the mountain this is.

nodes.description: Find blob-shaped features at a size

attrs.label: Blob size
attrs.tooltip:
The feature size to look for. This is a band-pass: blobs
much larger or smaller than this are ignored.

attrs.label: Strength
attrs.tooltip:
How strongly a blob must stand out from its surroundings
to be selected at all.

attrs.label: Hollows instead of bumps
attrs.tooltip:
Finds dips instead of bumps - the same detector run the
other way up.

nodes.description: A band along a mask's boundary

attrs.label: Threshold
attrs.tooltip:
The value that counts as inside the region whose border is
wanted.

attrs.label: Reach
attrs.tooltip: How wide the band along the boundary is.

attrs.label: Side
attrs.tooltip:
Whether the band lies inside the region, outside it, or
straddles the line. Inside is what you want to darken a
shore; outside to spill something past an edge.

nodes.description: Ambient-occlusion-like cavity map

attrs.label: Edge softness
attrs.tooltip:
How gradually the selection gives out at its edges.
Near zero gives a hard cut, which reads as drawn on; a
soft edge is what lets one material give way to
another.

attrs.label: Invert
attrs.tooltip:
Selects everything this node did not - the ground it
rejected becomes the mask.

attrs.label: Radius
attrs.tooltip:
How far the sampling reaches when deciding how enclosed a
point is. Larger radii find broad basins; small ones find
pits and crevices.

nodes.description: Select concave (valleys) or convex (ridges)

attrs.label: Edge softness
attrs.tooltip:
How gradually the selection gives out at its edges.
Near zero gives a hard cut, which reads as drawn on; a
soft edge is what lets one material give way to
another.

attrs.label: Invert
attrs.tooltip:
Selects everything this node did not - the ground it
rejected becomes the mask.

attrs.label: Mode
attrs.tooltip:
Concave picks the hollows - valley floors, gullies, the
places water and soil collect. Convex picks the ridges and
outcrops where they are stripped away.

attrs.label: Feature scale
attrs.tooltip:
How large a feature counts. Small scales find surface
crinkles; large ones find whole landforms.

nodes.description: Select the middle elevations

attrs.label: Edge softness
attrs.tooltip:
How gradually the selection gives out at its edges.
Near zero gives a hard cut, which reads as drawn on; a
soft edge is what lets one material give way to
another.

attrs.label: Invert
attrs.tooltip:
Selects everything this node did not - the ground it
rejected becomes the mask.

attrs.label: Center
attrs.tooltip:
The height the selection is centred on, as a fraction of
the terrain's range.

attrs.label: Width
attrs.tooltip:
How far either side of the centre is still selected. This
is the band-pass of the three altitude selectors: it takes
the middle ground and leaves the peaks and the floors.

nodes.description: Select by slope steepness

attrs.label: Edge softness
attrs.tooltip:
How gradually the selection gives out at its edges.
Near zero gives a hard cut, which reads as drawn on; a
soft edge is what lets one material give way to
another.

attrs.label: Invert
attrs.tooltip:
Selects everything this node did not - the ground it
rejected becomes the mask.

attrs.label: Slope band
attrs.tooltip:
The band of steepness that is selected, 1 being flat
ground and 0 a vertical face. Rock wants a low band,
meadow a high one.

nodes.description: Select where two surfaces trade places

attrs.label: Tolerance
attrs.tooltip:
How close two surfaces must come before the place they
meet is called a transition.

attrs.label: Invert
attrs.tooltip: Selects everywhere the two surfaces do not trade places.

nodes.description: Thin a mask to its centerlines

attrs.label: Threshold
attrs.tooltip:
The value above which a point counts as part of the region
being reduced to a centre line.

nodes.description: How deep into the shape each cell sits

attrs.label: Threshold
attrs.tooltip:
The value above which a point counts as part of the region
whose centre line the distance is measured from.

nodes.description: Ambient occlusion baked from a height input

attrs.label: Radius
attrs.tooltip:
How far around each point the surroundings are sampled to
decide how enclosed it is. Small radii darken creases and
pits; large ones darken whole valleys.

attrs.label: Strength
attrs.tooltip:
How dark the enclosed places get. Ambient occlusion is the
soft shadow of a surface against itself, and a little of
it does more for the sense of depth than any amount of
bump.

nodes.description: Derive normal + roughness maps from an albedo texture

attrs.label: Normal strength
attrs.tooltip:
How much relief is inferred from the photograph's
brightness. A photograph has no depth in it, so this is a
guess: too much and every dark patch becomes a dent.

attrs.label: Roughness base
attrs.tooltip:
The roughness the whole surface starts at, before the
picture varies it.

attrs.label: Roughness variation
attrs.tooltip:
How much the picture's own detail varies the roughness, so
darker, damper-looking areas come out glossier than pale
dry ones.

attrs.label: Bright = smooth
attrs.tooltip:
Swaps which end of the picture reads as glossy. If the
highlights are landing on the wrong parts of the surface,
this is the switch.

nodes.description: Pack three grayscale inputs into one RGB texture

attrs.label: Normalize inputs
attrs.tooltip:
Rescales the result to fill 0..1. Off keeps the raw
values, which is what you want when the output feeds
arithmetic rather than a blend.

nodes.description: Split a texture into red, green, blue, alpha and luminance masks
Color correction: brightness, contrast, saturation, hue, tint

attrs.label: Brightness
attrs.tooltip: Scales every colour up or down.

attrs.label: Contrast
attrs.tooltip: Pushes colours away from mid-grey, or toward it below 1.

attrs.label: Saturation
attrs.tooltip:
How strong the colour is. 0 leaves greyscale with all the
detail intact.

attrs.label: Hue shift °
attrs.tooltip:
Rotates every colour around the wheel, in degrees. A small
shift is the cheapest way to make one photographed surface
look like a different rock.

attrs.label: Tint R
attrs.tooltip:
Multiplies the red channel, for correcting a cast rather
than recolouring.

attrs.label: Tint G
attrs.tooltip: Multiplies the green channel.

attrs.label: Tint B
attrs.tooltip: Multiplies the blue channel.

nodes.description: Convex/concave curvature map from height

attrs.label: Feature scale
attrs.tooltip:
How large a feature the curvature is measured over. Small
finds surface crinkle; large finds whether you are on a
ridge or in a hollow.

attrs.label: Contrast
attrs.tooltip:
Stretches the result apart. Raw curvature bunches around
zero, so without this most of the map reads as flat.

nodes.description: Distribution layer: the presence that shades also places objects

attrs.label: Instances
attrs.tooltip: How many objects the presence places at full presence.

attrs.label: Min spacing
attrs.tooltip:
The closest two placed items may come to one another. This
is what stops a distribution clumping into overlapping
piles at high density.

attrs.label: Presence threshold
attrs.tooltip: Presence below this places nothing at all.

attrs.label: Instance size from
attrs.tooltip: The point value: the same for all, following the presence (strong presence, big plant), or many small and a few large.

nodes.description: Ecosystem layer: a population placed by the layer's presence, reacting to the layer below

attrs.label: Name
attrs.tooltip:
What this population is called in the stack and the
Objects tree.

attrs.label: Populate
attrs.tooltip:
Turns the layer off without removing it or losing its
settings.

attrs.label: Invert presence
attrs.tooltip:
Uses the mask the other way round: the layer appears where
the mask is dark.

attrs.label: Density (per hectare)
attrs.tooltip:
Instances per hectare (100 m x 100 m) at full presence.
A rate, not a count: the same setting fills a 1 km tile
and a 20 km one to the same look.

attrs.label: Minimum spacing (m)
attrs.tooltip:
The lattice the candidates stand on. Changing the density
never moves an instance; changing this reseeds them all.

attrs.label: Placement
attrs.tooltip:
How the candidate positions are laid out before anything
is rejected. A jittered lattice covers ground evenly;
purely random leaves clumps and bald patches, which is
sometimes what you want.

attrs.label: Clumping
attrs.tooltip: Groups instances together as species do in nature.

attrs.label: Clump size (m)
attrs.tooltip:
How far across one clump of plants is, in metres.
Vegetation gathers where the ground suits it, and a
population spread perfectly evenly is the clearest sign of
a generated one.

attrs.label: Populate around the camera
attrs.tooltip:
Off: the population covers the terrain tile, computed once.
On: it covers the ground wherever the camera goes - a planet
or an infinite terrain has no tile to cover - generated in
cells on demand and thrown away behind you. What a cell
holds never depends on where it was seen from.

attrs.label: Populate within (m)
attrs.tooltip:
How far from the camera the ground is populated when
'Populate around the camera' is on.

attrs.label: Terrain size (m)
attrs.tooltip:
The tile's width; the studio keeps this in step with the
project so the rate above means what it says.

attrs.label: Presence threshold
attrs.tooltip: Presence below this places nothing at all.

attrs.label: Slope influence
attrs.tooltip:
1: instances thin out on steep ground. 0: the same density
whatever the slope.

attrs.label: By altitude
attrs.tooltip: Limits the layer to a band of heights.

attrs.label: Range of altitudes
attrs.tooltip:
Whether the altitude band is read against the terrain's
own range, in absolute height units, or from sea level.

attrs.label: Altitude band
attrs.tooltip: As a fraction of the terrain's own height range.

attrs.label: Sea level
attrs.tooltip:
The height that counts as sea level, when the altitude
band is measured from it rather than from the terrain's
own range.

attrs.label: Fade
attrs.tooltip:
How gradually the layer gives out at the edges of its
altitude band. Zero draws a contour line across the
hillside.

attrs.label: By slope
attrs.tooltip: Limits the layer to a band of steepness.

attrs.label: Slope band
attrs.tooltip: Degrees from horizontal. 0 is flat, 90 is a cliff.

attrs.label: Fade
attrs.tooltip:
How gradually the layer gives out at the edges of its
slope band.

attrs.label: By orientation
attrs.tooltip: Limits the layer to slopes facing a particular way.

attrs.label: Faces
attrs.tooltip: Compass direction the surface looks towards. 0 is north.

attrs.label: Arc
attrs.tooltip:
How wide an arc of facings counts as the favoured
direction. Narrow puts moss on the north face alone; wide
covers most of the hill.

attrs.label: Fade
attrs.tooltip:
How gradually the layer gives out as a slope turns away
from the favoured direction.

attrs.label: Terrain height scale
attrs.tooltip:
World height of a heightmap unit as a fraction of the tile's
width; the studio keeps this in step with the project so a
slope in degrees is the slope the viewport shows.

attrs.label: Decay near objects
attrs.tooltip:
Thins the population around the objects standing on the
terrain (the 'objects' input: 0 at an object, 1 far away).
1 leaves a void right at them.

attrs.label: Reach
attrs.tooltip:
How far from the objects the decay extends, as a fraction
of the terrain.

attrs.label: Falloff
attrs.tooltip:
0 linear. Positive: the void is larger and more sudden.
Negative: gentler.

attrs.label: Affinity with layer below
attrs.tooltip:
Positive: instances gather around the instances of the
layer below (primroses around the trees) and thin out
elsewhere. Negative: everywhere except near them.

attrs.label: Affinity radius (m)
attrs.tooltip:
How far this population reaches to gather around the one
below it, in metres.

attrs.label: Repulsion from layer below
attrs.tooltip:
Sudden. Positive: a void around each instance below (no
grass under the canopy). Negative: only inside that void
(small stones at the foot of the boulder). Use both: near
the trees but not under them.

attrs.label: Repulsion radius (m)
attrs.tooltip:
How far this population is pushed back from the one below
it, in metres - the bare ring around the base of a tree.

attrs.label: Avoid overlapping instances
attrs.tooltip: No two instances closer than their footprints allow.

attrs.label: Species
attrs.tooltip:
How many kinds of object this layer places. Each scene
object bound to the layer picks the species it stands for.

attrs.label: Species 1 presence
attrs.tooltip:
Relative to the other species: raising every presence
places no more instances.

attrs.label: Species 1 scale
attrs.tooltip:
This species' size, as a multiple of the layer's own
overall scaling. A population of one mesh at several
sizes reads as a stand of different ages; every copy
identical reads as instancing.

attrs.label: Species 2 presence
attrs.tooltip:
Relative to the other species: raising every presence
places no more instances.

attrs.label: Species 2 scale
attrs.tooltip:
This species' size, as a multiple of the layer's own
overall scaling. A population of one mesh at several
sizes reads as a stand of different ages; every copy
identical reads as instancing.

attrs.label: Species 3 presence
attrs.tooltip:
Relative to the other species: raising every presence
places no more instances.

attrs.label: Species 3 scale
attrs.tooltip:
This species' size, as a multiple of the layer's own
overall scaling. A population of one mesh at several
sizes reads as a stand of different ages; every copy
identical reads as instancing.

attrs.label: Species 4 presence
attrs.tooltip:
Relative to the other species: raising every presence
places no more instances.

attrs.label: Species 4 scale
attrs.tooltip:
This species' size, as a multiple of the layer's own
overall scaling. A population of one mesh at several
sizes reads as a stand of different ages; every copy
identical reads as instancing.

attrs.label: Species 5 presence
attrs.tooltip:
Relative to the other species: raising every presence
places no more instances.

attrs.label: Species 5 scale
attrs.tooltip:
This species' size, as a multiple of the layer's own
overall scaling. A population of one mesh at several
sizes reads as a stand of different ages; every copy
identical reads as instancing.

attrs.label: Species 6 presence
attrs.tooltip:
Relative to the other species: raising every presence
places no more instances.

attrs.label: Species 6 scale
attrs.tooltip:
This species' size, as a multiple of the layer's own
overall scaling. A population of one mesh at several
sizes reads as a stand of different ages; every copy
identical reads as instancing.

attrs.label: Species 7 presence
attrs.tooltip:
Relative to the other species: raising every presence
places no more instances.

attrs.label: Species 7 scale
attrs.tooltip:
This species' size, as a multiple of the layer's own
overall scaling. A population of one mesh at several
sizes reads as a stand of different ages; every copy
identical reads as instancing.

attrs.label: Species 8 presence
attrs.tooltip:
Relative to the other species: raising every presence
places no more instances.

attrs.label: Species 8 scale
attrs.tooltip:
This species' size, as a multiple of the layer's own
overall scaling. A population of one mesh at several
sizes reads as a stand of different ages; every copy
identical reads as instancing.

attrs.label: Overall scaling
attrs.tooltip:
The size of one copy, as a multiple of the mesh's own
size.

attrs.label: Size variation
attrs.tooltip: 1: instances range from half to twice the size.

attrs.label: Keep proportions
attrs.tooltip: 1: the three axes scale together. 0: each on its own.

attrs.label: Direction from surface
attrs.tooltip:
0: instances grow vertically whatever the slope.
1: perpendicular to the ground (rocks); trees want 0.

attrs.label: Rotation
attrs.tooltip:
How far a copy may be turned about its up axis. Full
rotation is right for anything without a front; less keeps
a set of objects aligned.

attrs.label: Maximum angle
attrs.tooltip: As a fraction of a half turn either way.

attrs.label: Offset from surface (m)
attrs.tooltip: Negative buries the instance.

attrs.label: Footprint radius (m)
attrs.tooltip:
The ground one instance claims at scale 1; what overlap
avoidance and the layer above measure against.

attrs.label: Shrink at low density
attrs.tooltip:
Lone instances are smaller (negative: larger), as at the
edge of a wood.

attrs.label: Low-density radius (m)
attrs.tooltip:
How close to the population below a copy must be before it
is made smaller, in metres. This is what puts stunted
growth under a canopy rather than an abrupt edge.

attrs.label: Lean out at low density
attrs.tooltip:
Lone instances lean into the slope, as plants reaching
for light.

attrs.label: Color variation
attrs.tooltip:
How much copies differ in brightness from one another.
Identical tint across a whole population is the second
clearest sign of instancing, after identical size.

attrs.label: Time offset range (s)
attrs.tooltip:
Each instance's wind phase is shifted by up to this, so a
field sways as a crowd, not a marching army.

nodes.description: Effector layer: a typed influence field for other systems to read

attrs.label: Effector kind
attrs.tooltip: What this field means to the systems that read it. Pressure: trodden or loaded ground. Wind: local air movement. Light and Heat: exposure. Moisture: wetness. Custom: whatever a script assigns it.

attrs.label: Strength
attrs.tooltip: How strongly this layer pushes the layers below it around.

attrs.label: Falloff
attrs.tooltip: A power on the mask: above 1 the field concentrates where the mask is strongest, below 1 it spreads.

attrs.label: Invert
attrs.tooltip:
Pushes where it would have pulled, and the other way
about.

attrs.label: Tint the material by the field
attrs.tooltip: Blends the field into the colour so it can be seen in the viewport while it is being painted. Off, the material's colour passes through untouched.

nodes.description: Solid color material (procedural function + color)

attrs.label: Red
attrs.tooltip:
The red component, linear rather than sRGB: 0.5 here is
not the mid-grey you would pick in a paint program. That
matters when a value is matched against a photograph.

attrs.label: Green
attrs.tooltip: The green component, linear rather than sRGB.

attrs.label: Blue
attrs.tooltip: The blue component, linear rather than sRGB.

nodes.description: A fractal through a colour map: RGBA texture out, and the same pattern as a mask

attrs.label: Base noise
attrs.tooltip: The noise the fractal is built from.

attrs.label: Wavelength
attrs.tooltip: Size of the largest feature, in tile widths.

attrs.label: Iterations
attrs.tooltip: How many times the pattern is added at a smaller size.

attrs.label: Roughness
attrs.tooltip:
1 keeps the same detail at every scale. Lower is
smoother, higher is grittier.

attrs.label: Gain
attrs.tooltip: Contrast of the result.

attrs.label: Distortion
attrs.tooltip:
Smears the sampling position with a low-frequency noise,
which breaks up the lattice the noise sits on.

attrs.label: Shape
attrs.tooltip:
The shape the harmonics take - rolling, ridged or
billowed. As colour rather than terrain, ridges read as
veining and billows as mottling.

attrs.label: Warp by input
attrs.tooltip: How far the warp input displaces the sample position.

attrs.label: Bias
attrs.tooltip:
Moves the midpoint of the pattern: below 0.5 the colour
map's left end takes more of the surface.

attrs.label: Gain
attrs.tooltip:
Pushes values away from the middle. High values give
hard-edged patches rather than a smooth wash.

attrs.label: Colour map
attrs.tooltip:
Colour and alpha both come from here. A stop's alpha
becomes the texture's alpha, so one fractal can decide
a layer's look and its presence at the same time.

nodes.description: Recolor a texture through a gradient by luminance

attrs.label: Gradient
attrs.tooltip:
The colour ramp the incoming value is looked up in: 0
takes the left end, 1 the right. This is how a height, a
slope or a mask becomes colour.

attrs.label: Amount
attrs.tooltip: How much of the mapped colour replaces what came in.

nodes.description: Levels: remap input black/white/gamma to output range

attrs.label: Input black
attrs.tooltip:
Input values at or below this are pulled to black. Raising
it deepens the shadows and throws away whatever detail was
below it.

attrs.label: Input white
attrs.tooltip: Input values at or above this are pushed to white.

attrs.label: Gamma
attrs.tooltip:
Bends the midtones without moving the two ends. Below 1
darkens them, above 1 lifts them.

attrs.label: Output black
attrs.tooltip:
The darkest the result is allowed to be. Raising it lifts
the whole picture off black, which is what a hazy or dusty
surface actually does.

attrs.label: Output white
attrs.tooltip: The brightest the result is allowed to be.

attrs.label: Per channel
attrs.tooltip:
Off: operate on luminance and keep the hue.
On: apply the curve to R, G and B separately.

nodes.description: Grayscale mask or heightmap as a texture channel

attrs.label: Normalize
attrs.tooltip:
Rescales the mask to fill 0..1 before it becomes a
picture.

attrs.label: Scale
attrs.tooltip: Multiplies the mask on its way into the texture.

attrs.label: Offset
attrs.tooltip: Added to the mask on its way into the texture.

nodes.description: One layer of a material stack: its own maps, its own mask, and its own reaction to altitude, slope and orientation

attrs.label: Name
attrs.tooltip:
What this layer is called in the stack. Naming them is the
difference between a readable material and six rows of
'Layer'.

attrs.label: Visible
attrs.tooltip:
Turns the layer off without removing it or losing its
settings.

attrs.label: Opacity
attrs.tooltip:
Overall presence of the layer, within whatever the
environment constraints below already allow. It cannot
put the layer anywhere they exclude.

attrs.label: Blend
attrs.tooltip:
Normal: ordinary alpha-over.
Cover: colour switches without a ramp, only the normal
transitions, so the layer reads as sitting on top.
Colour only: takes colour from here, everything else
from below.

attrs.label: Invert mask
attrs.tooltip:
Uses the mask the other way round: the layer appears where
the mask is dark.

attrs.label: Roughness
attrs.tooltip: Used where this layer has no roughness map connected.

attrs.label: Add to normals below
attrs.tooltip:
1: this layer's relief adds to the layer beneath, the
way lichen sits on rock. 0: it replaces it, the way
snow flattens what it covers.

attrs.label: Displacement
attrs.tooltip:
Multiplies the displacement input - a FakeStones or
GrassDisplacement 'displacement' output, or any relief
in heightmap units - where this layer is present.

attrs.label: Add to displacement below
attrs.tooltip:
1 stacks this layer's relief on the layers below; 0
replaces theirs where this layer is present.

attrs.label: Alpha boost
attrs.tooltip:
The layer's overall presence, within what the
constraints below allow. Positive: stronger.

attrs.label: Highlight (solid color)
attrs.tooltip:
Shows the layer as a flat colour so you can see where
it lands. Shading is off while highlighted.

attrs.label: Highlight color
attrs.tooltip:
The flat colour the layer is shown in while Highlight is
on, so you can see exactly where it lands.

attrs.label: By altitude
attrs.tooltip: Limits the layer to a band of heights.

attrs.label: Range of altitudes
attrs.tooltip:
By terrain: the band is a fraction of this terrain's own
range. Absolute: in the terrain's height units. Relative
to sea: measured from the sea level below.

attrs.label: Altitude band
attrs.tooltip: As a fraction of the terrain's own height range.

attrs.label: Sea level
attrs.tooltip:
The height that counts as sea level, when the altitude
band is measured from it rather than from the terrain's
own range.

attrs.label: Fade
attrs.tooltip:
How gradually the layer gives out at the edges of its
altitude band. Zero draws a contour line across the
hillside.

attrs.label: By slope
attrs.tooltip: Limits the layer to a band of steepness.

attrs.label: Slope band
attrs.tooltip: Degrees from horizontal. 0 is flat, 90 is a cliff.

attrs.label: Fade
attrs.tooltip:
How gradually the layer gives out at the edges of its
slope band.

attrs.label: Height scale
attrs.tooltip:
The terrain's vertical scale, so 'By slope' and
'By orientation' read real degrees. Kept in step with
the project automatically.

attrs.label: By orientation
attrs.tooltip: Limits the layer to slopes facing a particular way.

attrs.label: Faces
attrs.tooltip:
Compass direction the surface looks towards, in degrees.
0 is north. North faces hold snow; south faces dry out.

attrs.label: Arc
attrs.tooltip: How far either side of that direction still counts.

attrs.label: Fade
attrs.tooltip:
How gradually the layer gives out as a slope turns away
from the favoured direction.

attrs.label: Tiling
attrs.tooltip:
How many times this layer's own maps repeat across the
terrain. Does not affect the mask or the constraints.

attrs.label: Offset
attrs.tooltip:
Slides this layer's own maps across the surface, without
moving the layers around it.

attrs.label: Rotation
attrs.tooltip:
Turns this layer's own maps. Rotating one layer of several
breaks the alignment that makes a stack read as printed.

nodes.description: The material: base color, normal, roughness, metallic, height and AO channels

attrs.label: Material name
attrs.tooltip:
What this material is called in the Objects tree and the
material browser. It is how you pick it when assigning it
to something.

attrs.label: Overall color
attrs.tooltip: Multiplies every colour in the material. White leaves it alone.

attrs.label: Brightness
attrs.tooltip:
Scales the whole colour up or down after everything
upstream. Use it to sit a material into a scene without
going back and editing the maps that made it.

attrs.label: Saturation
attrs.tooltip:
How strong the colour is. 0 leaves a greyscale surface
with all of its detail intact, which is often closer to
real weathered rock than the photograph it came from.

attrs.label: Color blend
attrs.tooltip: Blend the picture with a solid colour, in product mode.

attrs.label: Blend color
attrs.tooltip:
A colour mixed into the whole surface. This is the
quickest way to tint a shared material differently per
object - a wash of ochre over the same rock.

attrs.label: Blend amount
attrs.tooltip: How much of the blend colour is mixed in.

attrs.label: Color mask
attrs.tooltip: 0: the colour multiplies the picture. 1: it replaces it.

attrs.label: Global alpha
attrs.tooltip: Where no alpha map is connected. Alpha does not bend light; transparency does.

attrs.label: Alpha boost
attrs.tooltip: For a layer of a multi-layer material: its overall presence, within the limits the Presence tab sets.

attrs.label: Normal intensity
attrs.tooltip: How much of the normal map's vector is applied.

attrs.label: Bump depth
attrs.tooltip: The amount of bump. Negative turns bumps into holes.

attrs.label: Dependent on slope
attrs.tooltip: Higher bumps on steep faces than on flat ground, as on eroded terrain.

attrs.label: Invert normal map
attrs.tooltip:
Flips the green channel of the normal map. There are two
conventions for which way is up and they are visually
identical until the light moves - if the bumps read as
dents, this is the switch.

attrs.label: Displacement depth
attrs.tooltip: Height map displacement applied to the surface, in world units. Moves geometry, not only normals.

attrs.label: Displacement smoothing
attrs.tooltip:
Softens the displacement before it moves the surface,
without touching the colour. Use it when a height map is
noisier than the geometry can carry.

attrs.label: Lighting model
attrs.tooltip: GGX: the physically based microfacet model, size is roughness. Phong: the legacy model, size and intensity independent.

attrs.label: Highlight intensity
attrs.tooltip:
How bright the direct highlight is. This is the sheen a
light leaves on the surface, as against Reflectivity
below, which is how much of the surroundings it mirrors.

attrs.label: Roughness (highlight size)
attrs.tooltip: Small: a polished surface with tight bright spots. Large: dull. Also multiplies a connected roughness map.

attrs.label: Highlight color
attrs.tooltip: A uniform shade for the highlights - blue for pearl.

attrs.label: Anisotropy
attrs.tooltip: Stretched highlights along a direction, for brushed metal or hair.

attrs.label: Global transparency
attrs.tooltip: How much light passes straight through. 0 is opaque.

attrs.label: Refraction index
attrs.tooltip: 1 air, 1.33 water, 1.52 glass. Bends light crossing the surface; also sets how reflective a transparent surface is.

attrs.label: Turn reflective with angle
attrs.tooltip: Glass and water mirror at a low angle. About 0.4 looks right.

attrs.label: Fade out
attrs.tooltip:
How much the surface thins toward its silhouette, so an
edge dissolves rather than ending on a hard line.

attrs.label: Thin surface (no refraction)
attrs.tooltip:
Treats the surface as having no thickness, so light passes
through without bending. Right for glass panes, leaves and
water films; wrong for a solid body of water, which does
refract.

attrs.label: Additive
attrs.tooltip: Adds the colour to the background: luminous, immaterial objects.

attrs.label: Flare intensity
attrs.tooltip: Brightening when light is seen through a partly transparent surface. Strongest at 50% transparency.

attrs.label: Flare span
attrs.tooltip:
How far the highlight spreads. Narrow reads as polished,
wide as satin.

attrs.label: Global reflectivity
attrs.tooltip:
How much of the surroundings the surface mirrors. Distinct
from the highlight: this is the world reflected, that is
the light source.

attrs.label: Minimal reflectivity
attrs.tooltip: Reflectivity looking straight at the surface; the angle sensitivity raises it toward grazing.

attrs.label: Sensitivity to incidence angle
attrs.tooltip:
How much more reflective the surface becomes at a grazing
angle. Nearly every real material does this - it is why a
wet road mirrors the sky ahead but not underfoot - so 0
reads as wrong.

attrs.label: Blurred reflections
attrs.tooltip:
How blurred the reflection is. 0 is a mirror; higher is
brushed metal or rippled water.

attrs.label: Metalness
attrs.tooltip: Metal reflects its own colour and has no diffuse. Also multiplies a connected metallic map.

attrs.label: Specular level (PBR)
attrs.tooltip: F0 of the non-metal parts: 0.5 is the common 4 %, 1 is 8 %.

attrs.label: Translucency
attrs.tooltip: Light bleeding through thin material toward the viewer.

attrs.label: Subsurface scattering
attrs.tooltip:
Lets light enter the surface, scatter inside and leave
elsewhere. This is what makes skin, wax, marble and snow
look lit from within rather than merely lit.

attrs.label: Average depth (m)
attrs.tooltip: How far light travels inside: a fraction of a millimetre for skin, centimetres for wax.

attrs.label: Absorption / scattering balance
attrs.tooltip:
Whether light inside the surface is mostly absorbed or
mostly scattered onward. Toward absorption gives dense,
waxy material; toward scattering gives translucent,
glowing material.

attrs.label: Scattering color
attrs.tooltip: The colour light picks up inside - the red of a finger over a torch.

attrs.label: Backlight
attrs.tooltip: Thin enough that light shows through from behind, like a leaf.

attrs.label: Coat intensity
attrs.tooltip: A thin reflective layer on top: the lacquer over car paint.

attrs.label: Coat tint
attrs.tooltip:
The colour of the clear coat over the surface - the
lacquer on car paint, the wet film on a stone. It reflects
and tints without changing the material underneath.

attrs.label: Coat roughness
attrs.tooltip:
How polished the clear coat is, independently of the
surface under it. A rough stone under a smooth wet coat is
exactly what a rock in a stream is.

attrs.label: Coat refraction index
attrs.tooltip:
The coat's refractive index, which sets how strongly it
reflects at a glancing angle. 1.5 is a lacquer or a
varnish; 1.33 is water.

attrs.label: Flatten
attrs.tooltip: 1: the coat has its own smooth normal. 0: it follows the bumps below.

attrs.label: Diffuse lighting
attrs.tooltip: How the material reacts to light from light sources. Diffuse + ambient should stay at 100%.

attrs.label: Ambient lighting
attrs.tooltip:
How much of the surrounding sky light the surface picks up
where nothing shines on it directly. Too low makes the
shadows read as black holes.

attrs.label: Luminous
attrs.tooltip: Seems to emit light. Does not cast real light.

attrs.label: Luminous color
attrs.tooltip:
Light the surface emits by itself. It lights nothing else
in the viewport - this is the surface glowing, not a lamp.

attrs.label: Contrast
attrs.tooltip: How fast the surface goes from light to shadow; low for fluffy things.

attrs.label: Color reflected light
attrs.tooltip: Highlights and reflections take the surface colour: metal.

attrs.label: Color transmitted light
attrs.tooltip: Light crossing a transparent surface takes its colour: stained glass.

attrs.label: Casts shadows
attrs.tooltip:
Whether the surface blocks light. Turning it off is a
lighting cheat, useful for glass and for foliage cards
that would otherwise shadow themselves into mud.

attrs.label: Receives shadows
attrs.tooltip: Whether other things can cast shadows onto this surface.

attrs.label: One sided
attrs.tooltip: Traced for one intersection per ray; matters for transparent surfaces.

attrs.label: Hide from camera rays
attrs.tooltip: Seen only in reflections and refractions.

attrs.label: Hide from reflected / refracted rays
attrs.tooltip:
Keeps the surface out of reflections and refractions while
leaving it visible to the camera. A compositing
convenience, not physics.

attrs.label: Ignore lighting
attrs.tooltip: No sun, no lights: the surface shows its own colour.

attrs.label: Ignore atmosphere
attrs.tooltip: No fog or haze between it and the camera.

attrs.label: Only shadows
attrs.tooltip: Invisible, but still casts a shadow.

attrs.label: Disable anti-aliasing
attrs.tooltip:
Turns off edge smoothing for this material. Only wanted
where a hard pixel boundary is the point, such as an index
or ID pass.

attrs.label: Mapping
attrs.tooltip: How the 2D maps wrap a 3D object. Terrain is always Flat (projected from above); the others are for objects.

attrs.label: Scale of the maps
attrs.tooltip: Scales every texture map together.

attrs.label: Origin
attrs.tooltip: Offsets the material in map space, for precise placement.

attrs.label: Rotation
attrs.tooltip: Turns the maps about the surface normal, in degrees.

attrs.label: Turbulence
attrs.tooltip: A noise repeatedly displaces where the maps are read, so a tiled picture stops looking tiled.

attrs.label: Complexity
attrs.tooltip:
How many scales of small-scale disturbance ripple the
surface normal. This is shading detail only - it does not
move the geometry.

attrs.label: Amplitude
attrs.tooltip:
How strongly the disturbance tilts the surface normal. A
little breaks up a surface that reads as too clean; a lot
looks like hammered metal.

attrs.label: Scale
attrs.tooltip:
How fine the disturbance is, in repeats across the
surface.

attrs.label: Harmonics
attrs.tooltip: How scale and amplitude shrink with each repetition of the noise.

attrs.label: Cycling
attrs.tooltip: A large, slow perturbation that keeps a material from repeating.

nodes.description: Blend up to six material layers by mask, height-aware, into albedo + roughness

attrs.label: Mixing
attrs.tooltip:
Weighted: every layer by its own mask. Two materials:
material 1 and 2 by one distribution (mask 1) against
the proportions, as Vue mixes.

attrs.label: Mixing proportions
attrs.tooltip: Left: more of material 1. Right: more of material 2.

attrs.label: Smooth blending strip
attrs.tooltip: The width of the band where the two are blended.

attrs.label: Blending method
attrs.tooltip: How the layers of the stack are combined into one surface.

attrs.label: Distribution dependent on environment
attrs.tooltip:
Whether the layers are allowed to react to altitude, slope
and orientation at all. Off, they blend by their masks
alone.

attrs.label: Influence of altitude
attrs.tooltip: Positive: material 2 higher up. Negative: lower down.

attrs.label: Influence of slope
attrs.tooltip: Positive: material 2 on steep faces. Negative: on flat.

attrs.label: Influence of orientation
attrs.tooltip:
How strongly the direction a slope faces counts toward
which layer shows. This is what puts moss on the north
face and dry grass on the south.

attrs.label: Azimuth
attrs.tooltip: Material 2 gathers on faces looking this way. 0 is north.

attrs.label: Height blend
attrs.tooltip:
0: plain weighted mix. 1: the layer whose texture is
highest at this texel wins — silt fills the cracks of
the rock before it covers the ridges.

attrs.label: Blend depth
attrs.tooltip: How far below the winning layer others still show.

attrs.label: Roughness
attrs.tooltip:
How rough this layer's surface is: 0 is a mirror, 1
is matt. Wet rock and ice sit low, dry scree and
grass high, and the difference between them is most
of what tells one layer from another when they are
the same colour.

attrs.label: Roughness
attrs.tooltip:
How rough this layer's surface is: 0 is a mirror, 1
is matt. Wet rock and ice sit low, dry scree and
grass high, and the difference between them is most
of what tells one layer from another when they are
the same colour.

attrs.label: Roughness
attrs.tooltip:
How rough this layer's surface is: 0 is a mirror, 1
is matt. Wet rock and ice sit low, dry scree and
grass high, and the difference between them is most
of what tells one layer from another when they are
the same colour.

attrs.label: Roughness
attrs.tooltip:
How rough this layer's surface is: 0 is a mirror, 1
is matt. Wet rock and ice sit low, dry scree and
grass high, and the difference between them is most
of what tells one layer from another when they are
the same colour.

attrs.label: Roughness
attrs.tooltip:
How rough this layer's surface is: 0 is a mirror, 1
is matt. Wet rock and ice sit low, dry scree and
grass high, and the difference between them is most
of what tells one layer from another when they are
the same colour.

attrs.label: Roughness
attrs.tooltip:
How rough this layer's surface is: 0 is a mirror, 1
is matt. Wet rock and ice sit low, dry scree and
grass high, and the difference between them is most
of what tells one layer from another when they are
the same colour.

nodes.description: Natural grain: one or two colours varied by a noise, for ground and rock

attrs.label: Base color
attrs.tooltip: The first of the two colours the grain runs between.

attrs.label: Mix with a second color
attrs.tooltip:
Off, the grain varies only in brightness. On, it runs
between two colours, which is how granite gets its mixed
mineral speckle.

attrs.label: Second color
attrs.tooltip: The second colour, when two are used.

attrs.label: Scale
attrs.tooltip: The overall size of the grain. Keep it large for a terrain, small for a pebble.

attrs.label: Roughness
attrs.tooltip: How much fine detail rides on the large variation.

attrs.label: Contrast
attrs.tooltip:
How sharply the grain separates. Low is a soft mottle;
high gives distinct grains against a background.

attrs.label: Balance
attrs.tooltip: Which of the two colours dominates.

attrs.label: Distortion
attrs.tooltip: Warps the grain so it stops looking like a noise.

nodes.description: Combine two normal maps (whiteout blend)

attrs.label: Detail strength
attrs.tooltip:
How much of the detail normal is laid over the base one.
The two are combined so the fine map rides on the coarse
one rather than replacing its direction.

nodes.description: A PBR material set (albedo/normal/roughness/AO): a folder of maps on disk, or a CC0 photoscan downloaded from ambientCG

attrs.label: Source
attrs.tooltip:
Where the maps come from. A folder holds the set's images; the
maps are found by name (color/albedo/diffuse, normal, roughness,
ao/ambientocclusion) - the layout every PBR library ships.

attrs.label: Material folder (or any map in it)
attrs.tooltip:
Pick any image of the set; the folder it is in is scanned for
the other maps.

attrs.label: ambientCG asset ID
attrs.tooltip:
Which surface from the library. Each brings its own
colour, normal, roughness and height maps together,
already matched.

attrs.label: Resolution
attrs.tooltip:
Which size of the maps to load. Lower costs less memory
and is invisible at a distance; the highest is for
surfaces the camera comes close to.

attrs.label: Mapping
attrs.tooltip:
How the maps are laid onto the surface. Triplanar projects
from three directions and blends, which is what stops the
stretching on a cliff face.

attrs.label: Tiles across
attrs.tooltip:
How many times the surface repeats. Photographed materials
show their repeat if this is pushed too high.

nodes.description: Compose albedo from a splatmap and up to 4 layer textures
Pack up to 4 masks into RGBA splat weights (normalized)

attrs.label: Normalize weights
attrs.tooltip:
Rescales the four channels so they sum to one at every
point. Splat weights that do not sum to one either darken
the surface or blow it out.

nodes.description: Blend two textures by mask / mode / opacity

attrs.label: Mode
attrs.tooltip: How the two pictures are combined.

attrs.label: Opacity
attrs.tooltip: How much of the second picture shows over the first.

nodes.description: Load an image texture (PNG/JPG/TGA/BMP) with mapping modes

attrs.label: Image file
attrs.tooltip:
The image file. Colour maps are read as sRGB and
everything else as linear, so a normal or roughness map
loaded here is not silently gamma-corrected.

attrs.label: Mapping
attrs.tooltip:
How the picture is laid onto the surface. Flat projection
is fine on ground seen from above; triplanar projects from
three directions and blends, which is what stops the
stretching on a cliff face.

attrs.label: Tiles across
attrs.tooltip:
How many times the picture repeats across the surface.
High counts show the repeat unless the picture was made
seamless.

attrs.label: Brightness
attrs.tooltip: Scales the picture after loading.

attrs.label: Gamma
attrs.tooltip: Gamma correction for this picture, overriding the global setting.

attrs.label: Rotate
attrs.tooltip: Turns the picture on the surface.

attrs.label: Invert colors
attrs.tooltip:
Flips the picture's values. On a height or roughness map
this turns bumps into dents and gloss into matt.

attrs.label: Mirror X
attrs.tooltip:
Mirrors alternate repeats across, which hides the seam of
a picture that does not tile.

attrs.label: Mirror Y
attrs.tooltip: Mirrors alternate repeats down.

attrs.label: Picture scale
attrs.tooltip: Multiplies the picture's values after loading.

attrs.label: Image offset
attrs.tooltip: Added to the picture's values after loading.

attrs.label: Interpolation
attrs.tooltip:
How the picture is sampled between its pixels. Smooth is
right for nearly everything; nearest keeps hard pixel
edges, which is what an index or ID map needs.

nodes.description: Texture luminance back into a mask/heightmap

attrs.label: Channel
attrs.tooltip:
Which channel of the picture becomes the mask. Luminance
is the usual choice; the single channels are for pictures
that were packed with a different mask in each one.

nodes.description: Tile, scale, offset and rotate a texture

attrs.label: Tiles
attrs.tooltip: How many times the picture repeats across the surface.

attrs.label: Offset
attrs.tooltip: Slides the picture across the surface.

attrs.label: Rotation
attrs.tooltip: Turns the picture on the surface.

attrs.label: Mirror repeat
attrs.tooltip: Flips alternate tiles so seams are less visible.

nodes.description: Blend two heightmaps (many modes)

attrs.label: Mode
attrs.tooltip:
How the two inputs are combined. Add and multiply are the
workhorses; max and min take whichever input is higher or
lower at each point, which keeps both shapes rather than
averaging them into mush.

attrs.label: Factor
attrs.tooltip:
The balance between the two inputs, where the mode uses
one.

attrs.label: Smooth k
attrs.tooltip:
Rounds the seam where max or min switches from one input
to the other. A hard switch leaves a crease that catches
the light as a line; this is the difference between two
terrains meeting and two terrains merging.

nodes.description: Per-pixel math on one input

attrs.label: Operation
attrs.tooltip: The arithmetic applied to every point.

attrs.label: Value
attrs.tooltip:
The constant the operation uses when nothing is wired to
the second input.

attrs.label: Invert blend
attrs.tooltip:
Applies this node where the blend input is dark instead of
where it is bright.

nodes.description: Derivatives: dx, dy, slope magnitude, laplacian
Height-stack: stack up to 4 layers by max

attrs.label: Blend softness
attrs.tooltip:
Rounds the seam where one layer gives way to the next, so
stacked terrains merge rather than meeting at a crease.

nodes.description: Carves along a drawn path - riverbeds, road cuts, canyons; negative depth builds walls

attrs.label: Points
attrs.tooltip:
The path, as x,z pairs in tile coordinates (0..1),
separated by spaces. Edit here, or ask the AI to
"draw a river from the northwest to the sea".

attrs.label: Smoothing
attrs.tooltip:
Chaikin corner-cutting passes: 0 keeps the polyline's
corners, a few make a flowing curve.

attrs.label: Closed loop
attrs.tooltip:
Joins the last point back to the first, so the path is a
loop.

attrs.label: Width
attrs.tooltip:
Half the carve reaches this far from the line, as a
fraction of the tile.

attrs.label: Depth
attrs.tooltip:
How deep the centre cuts below the surface. Negative
raises instead: walls, levees, causeways.

attrs.label: Profile
attrs.tooltip:
The cross-section: U for rivers, V for gorges, a flat
bed with shoulders for roads and canals.

attrs.label: Grade along the path
attrs.tooltip:
0 follows the terrain exactly - the cut is everywhere
the same depth. 1 grades the bed toward the path's
smoothed height, the way water and roadbuilders do,
cutting deeper through rises and shallower in dips.

attrs.label: Remap to range
attrs.tooltip:
Rescales the result so its lowest point sits at the
bottom of the range below and its highest at the top.
Off keeps the raw values, which is what you want when
a node feeds arithmetic rather than a picture.

attrs.label: Output range
attrs.tooltip:
The low and high the result is rescaled into. 0..1 is
the terrain's own range; a narrower band makes this
node a gentler contribution when it is added to
another.

attrs.label: Invert
attrs.tooltip:
Turns the result upside down within its range - peaks
become hollows. Applied after the remap.

attrs.label: Gain (gamma)
attrs.tooltip:
Bends the result toward its low or high end. Below 1
lifts the middle, so more of the map sits high; above
1 pushes it down, so peaks become sparser and sharper.

attrs.label: Zero edges width
attrs.tooltip:
Fades the terrain to zero at the borders over this
fraction of the map — clean edges for islands/tiles.

attrs.label: Invert blend

Applies this node where the blend input is dark instead of
where it is bright.

nodes.description: Route a path across the terrain

attrs.label: Start
attrs.tooltip: Where the route begins, as a fraction of the tile.

attrs.label: End
attrs.tooltip: Where it ends.

attrs.label: Slope penalty
attrs.tooltip:
How much climbing costs against walking flat. High
values contour around hills the way real roads do.

attrs.label: Keep every Nth point
attrs.tooltip:
Keeps only every Nth point of the found route. The search
returns a point per cell, which is far more than a road or
a river needs.

nodes.description: Midpoint-displace a path into a wander

attrs.label: Iterations
attrs.tooltip:
How many times each segment is split and its midpoint
pushed aside. Each pass doubles the detail, so a few turn
a straight line into a natural wander.

attrs.label: Amplitude
attrs.tooltip: How far the midpoints are pushed.

nodes.description: Even spacing along a path

attrs.label: Spacing
attrs.tooltip:
How far apart the resampled points are, as a fraction of
the tile.

attrs.label: Smoothing
attrs.tooltip: How much the path is smoothed as it is resampled.

nodes.description: How far every point lies from a path, as a field to mask or displace with

attrs.label: Reach
attrs.tooltip: How far from the path its influence extends.

attrs.label: Invert
attrs.tooltip:
Measures the distance the other way, so the field is high
on the path rather than away from it.

attrs.label: Closed loop
attrs.tooltip: Treats the path as a loop.

attrs.label: Smoothing
attrs.tooltip: How much the distance field is smoothed.

nodes.description: A smooth curve through the points

attrs.label: Samples per segment
attrs.tooltip:
How many points are generated along each original segment.
More gives a smoother curve and a heavier cloud.

attrs.label: Tension
attrs.tooltip:
How tightly the curve hugs its control points. Low sweeps
wide between them; high pulls it close and can overshoot.

nodes.description: Order a point cloud into a path
Keep points by mask and chance

attrs.label: Mask band
attrs.tooltip: The range of values a point must carry to be kept.

attrs.label: Keep fraction
attrs.tooltip:
Whether points inside the band are the ones kept or the
ones dropped.

nodes.description: Read points from a CSV file

attrs.label: File
attrs.tooltip: The CSV file to read points from. One row per point.

nodes.description: Attract to, repel from another cloud; keep instances from overlapping

attrs.label: Affinity with layer below
attrs.tooltip:
Positive: instances gather around the instances of the
layer below (primroses around the trees) and thin out
elsewhere. Negative: everywhere except near them.

attrs.label: Affinity radius (m)
attrs.tooltip:
How far this population reaches to gather around the one
below it, in metres.

attrs.label: Repulsion from layer below
attrs.tooltip:
Sudden. Positive: a void around each instance below (no
grass under the canopy). Negative: only inside that void
(small stones at the foot of the boulder). Use both: near
the trees but not under them.

attrs.label: Repulsion radius (m)
attrs.tooltip:
How far this population is pushed back from the one below
it, in metres - the bare ring around the base of a tree.

attrs.label: Avoid overlapping instances
attrs.tooltip: No two instances closer than their footprints allow.

attrs.label: Terrain size (m)
attrs.tooltip:
The tile's width in metres, so the distances above mean
real metres. The studio keeps this in step with the
project.

nodes.description: Combines two point clouds into one, keeping the attributes of both

attrs.label: Drop B closer than
attrs.tooltip:

any A point is dropped - A has right of way.

nodes.description: Pushes points apart until they are evenly spaced, taking the clumps out of a random scatter

attrs.label: Iterations
attrs.tooltip:
How many times the points push each other apart. More
approaches an even spacing; a few passes take the worst
clumps out and leave the scatter looking natural.

attrs.label: Strength
attrs.tooltip: How hard each pass pushes.

nodes.description: Distance to the nearest point

attrs.label: Reach
attrs.tooltip: How far from a point its influence extends.

attrs.label: Invert
attrs.tooltip:
Measures distance the other way, so the field is high near

nodes.description: Point values from the terrain

attrs.label: Normalize 0..1

attrs.tooltip:
The shape stamped at each point. A soft falloff blends

attrs.label: Radius
attrs.tooltip: How large each stamp is.

attrs.label: Amplitude
attrs.tooltip: How strong each stamp is.

attrs.label: Scale by point value
attrs.tooltip:
Sizes each stamp by the value the point carries, so a
cloud that already knows how big each thing is can say so.

attrs.label: Blend
attrs.tooltip:
How overlapping stamps combine. Add piles them up, which
counts density; max keeps them at one, which draws
coverage.

attrs.label: Overall scaling
attrs.tooltip:
The size of one copy, as a multiple of the mesh's own
size.

attrs.label: Size variation
attrs.tooltip: 1: instances range from half to twice the size.

attrs.label: Keep proportions
attrs.tooltip: 1: the three axes scale together. 0: each on its own.

attrs.label: Direction from surface
attrs.tooltip:
0: instances grow vertically whatever the slope.
1: perpendicular to the ground (rocks); trees want 0.

attrs.label: Rotation
attrs.tooltip:
How far a copy may be turned about its up axis. Full
rotation is right for anything without a front; less keeps
a set of objects aligned.

attrs.label: Maximum angle
attrs.tooltip: As a fraction of a half turn either way.

attrs.label: Offset from surface (m)
attrs.tooltip: Negative buries the instance.

attrs.label: Footprint radius (m)
attrs.tooltip:
The ground one instance claims at scale 1; what overlap
avoidance and the layer above measure against.

attrs.label: Shrink at low density
attrs.tooltip:
Lone instances are smaller (negative: larger), as at the
edge of a wood.

attrs.label: Low-density radius (m)
attrs.tooltip:
How close to the population below a copy must be before it
is made smaller, in metres. This is what puts stunted
growth under a canopy rather than an abrupt edge.

attrs.label: Lean out at low density
attrs.tooltip:
Lone instances lean into the slope, as plants reaching
for light.

attrs.label: Color variation
attrs.tooltip:
How much copies differ in brightness from one another.
Identical tint across a whole population is the second
clearest sign of instancing, after identical size.

attrs.label: Time offset range (s)
attrs.tooltip:
Each instance's wind phase is shifted by up to this, so a
field sways as a crowd, not a marching army.

attrs.label: Terrain size (m)
attrs.tooltip:
The tile's width in metres, so the distances above mean
real metres. The studio keeps this in step with the
project.

nodes.description: Scatter by density per hectare and the presence of the ground

attrs.label: Invert presence
attrs.tooltip:
Uses the presence mask the other way round: things are
placed where it is dark.

attrs.label: Density (per hectare)
attrs.tooltip:
Instances per hectare (100 m x 100 m) at full presence.
A rate, not a count: the same setting fills a 1 km tile
and a 20 km one to the same look.

attrs.label: Minimum spacing (m)
attrs.tooltip:
The lattice the candidates stand on. Changing the density
never moves an instance; changing this reseeds them all.

attrs.label: Placement
attrs.tooltip:
How the candidate positions are laid out before anything
is rejected. A jittered lattice covers ground evenly;
purely random leaves clumps and bald patches, which is
sometimes what you want.

attrs.label: Clumping
attrs.tooltip: Groups instances together as species do in nature.

attrs.label: Clump size (m)
attrs.tooltip:
How far across one clump of plants is, in metres.
Vegetation gathers where the ground suits it, and a
population spread perfectly evenly is the clearest sign of
a generated one.

attrs.label: Populate around the camera
attrs.tooltip:
Off: the population covers the terrain tile, computed once.
On: it covers the ground wherever the camera goes - a planet
or an infinite terrain has no tile to cover - generated in
cells on demand and thrown away behind you. What a cell
holds never depends on where it was seen from.

attrs.label: Populate within (m)
attrs.tooltip:
How far from the camera the ground is populated when
'Populate around the camera' is on.

attrs.label: Terrain size (m)
attrs.tooltip:
The tile's width; the studio keeps this in step with the
project so the rate above means what it says.

attrs.label: Presence threshold
attrs.tooltip: Presence below this places nothing at all.

attrs.label: Slope influence
attrs.tooltip:
1: instances thin out on steep ground. 0: the same density
whatever the slope.

attrs.label: By altitude
attrs.tooltip: Limits the layer to a band of heights.

attrs.label: Range of altitudes
attrs.tooltip:
Whether the altitude band is read against the terrain's
own range, in absolute height units, or from sea level.

attrs.label: Altitude band
attrs.tooltip: As a fraction of the terrain's own height range.

attrs.label: Sea level
attrs.tooltip:
The height that counts as sea level, when the altitude
band is measured from it rather than from the terrain's
own range.

attrs.label: Fade
attrs.tooltip:
How gradually the layer gives out at the edges of its
altitude band. Zero draws a contour line across the
hillside.

attrs.label: By slope
attrs.tooltip: Limits the layer to a band of steepness.

attrs.label: Slope band
attrs.tooltip: Degrees from horizontal. 0 is flat, 90 is a cliff.

attrs.label: Fade
attrs.tooltip:
How gradually the layer gives out at the edges of its
slope band.

attrs.label: By orientation
attrs.tooltip: Limits the layer to slopes facing a particular way.

attrs.label: Faces
attrs.tooltip: Compass direction the surface looks towards. 0 is north.

attrs.label: Arc
attrs.tooltip:
How wide an arc of facings counts as the favoured
direction. Narrow puts moss on the north face alone; wide
covers most of the hill.

attrs.label: Fade
attrs.tooltip:
How gradually the layer gives out as a slope turns away
from the favoured direction.

attrs.label: Terrain height scale
attrs.tooltip:
World height of a heightmap unit as a fraction of the tile's
width; the studio keeps this in step with the project so a
slope in degrees is the slope the viewport shows.

attrs.label: Decay near objects
attrs.tooltip:
Thins the population around the objects standing on the
terrain (the 'objects' input: 0 at an object, 1 far away).
1 leaves a void right at them.

attrs.label: Reach
attrs.tooltip:
How far from the objects the decay extends, as a fraction
of the terrain.

attrs.label: Falloff
attrs.tooltip:
0 linear. Positive: the void is larger and more sudden.
Negative: gentler.

attrs.tooltip: How many points are scattered.

attrs.tooltip:

attrs.label: Min spacing
attrs.tooltip:
The closest two points may come, for the spaced mode. This

attrs.label: Value distribution
attrs.tooltip:
The per-point value stream: uniform 0..1, a power law
(many small, few large - natural size mixes), or
Weibull (clustered around a typical size).

attrs.label: Distribution shape
attrs.tooltip:
How the spacing is enforced - a hard exclusion around each
point, or a softer falling-off preference.

attrs.label: Height steps
attrs.tooltip:
Each column's flat top snaps to one of this many
levels, the way cooling lava fractures in tiers.

attrs.label: Crack width
attrs.tooltip:
How wide the joint between neighbouring columns is,
as a fraction of a column. Also drives the second

attrs.label: Crack depth
attrs.tooltip:

their steep slip face is on the downwind side -

going.

attrs.tooltip:

attrs.tooltip:
Stone size as a fraction of terrain width;

attrs.label: Stone density
attrs.tooltip:
The share of lattice cells that hold a stone. This
node writes into the heightmap, so its smallest
possible stone is a couple of texels - about 14 m on
a 5 km tile. For stones you can stand next to, use

attrs.tooltip:
A stone's height as a fraction of its radius. Every

down. Few gives a handful of broad steps; many
averages into smooth rolling ground.

the map. 0 gives hard cliffs at every fault line.

nodes.description: Oriented sparse-kernel noise (streaked rock)

attrs.label: Octaves
attrs.tooltip:
How many sizes of kernel are layered. Gabor noise is
expensive per octave, so this stops at 6 where the
other noises go to 16.

attrs.label: Kernel frequency
attrs.tooltip:
How many waves are packed inside each kernel. This
is the pitch of the grain, as against Scale below,
which is how large a patch of it is.

attrs.label: Orientation °
attrs.tooltip:
Which way the grain runs, when Anisotropy is high
enough for it to have a direction at all.

attrs.label: Anisotropy
attrs.tooltip:
1 locks every kernel to the orientation - streaks.
0 draws orientations at random - isotropic grain.

attrs.label: Scale
attrs.tooltip:
How many kernel cells fit across the tile - the size
of the pattern, as against Kernel frequency, which
is the pitch of the grain inside it.

attrs.label: Flavor
attrs.tooltip:
Phasor keeps only the phase of the kernel field, so
the wave profile stays crisp everywhere - sawtooth
reads as bedding planes, square as strata steps.

attrs.label: Remap to range
attrs.tooltip:
Rescales the result so its lowest point sits at the
bottom of the range below and its highest at the top.
Off keeps the raw values, which is what you want when
a node feeds arithmetic rather than a picture.

attrs.label: Output range
attrs.tooltip:
The low and high the result is rescaled into. 0..1 is
the terrain's own range; a narrower band makes this
node a gentler contribution when it is added to
another.

attrs.label: Invert
attrs.tooltip:
Turns the result upside down within its range - peaks
become hollows. Applied after the remap.

attrs.label: Gain (gamma)
attrs.tooltip:
Bends the result toward its low or high end. Below 1
lifts the middle, so more of the map sits high; above
1 pushes it down, so peaks become sparser and sharper.

attrs.label: Zero edges width
attrs.tooltip:
Fades the terrain to zero at the borders over this
fraction of the map — clean edges for islands/tiles.

attrs.label: Raggedness
attrs.tooltip: How uneven the tops of the tufts are.

attrs.label: Grows on slopes
attrs.tooltip:
Grass takes only ground whose slope is inside this band

attrs.label: Slope fade
attrs.tooltip:
How gradually the grass gives out at the edge of the
slope band. Zero gives a hard line across the
hillside, which reads as drawn on.

particular thing in a particular place rather than

nodes.description: Coherent noise: fBm, ridged, billow, swiss, value, cellular

attrs.label: Type
attrs.tooltip:
Which noise the octaves are built from. Perlin fBm
is rolling ground; Ridged gives sharp crests and is
the usual starting point for mountains; Billow the
rounded lumps of weathered rock; Swiss adds an
erosion-like warp to the ridges. The Worley family
is cellular - F1 for blobs, edges for a crack
network.

attrs.label: Octaves
attrs.tooltip:
How many times the pattern is added at a smaller
size. Each adds finer detail and costs about as
much again; once an octave is finer than a texel it
buys nothing.

attrs.label: Lacunarity
attrs.tooltip:
How much smaller each octave is than the last. 2
halves it, which is the usual choice; higher leaves
a gap between the scales and reads as two separate
patterns rather than one surface.

attrs.label: Gain
attrs.tooltip:
How much of its predecessor's strength each octave
keeps. Low is smooth and dominated by the largest
forms; high is uniformly rough at every scale.

attrs.label: Ridge weight
attrs.tooltip:
Ridged and Swiss only: how strongly a high octave is
suppressed where the one below it was already high.
This is what keeps detail in the valleys and off the
crests, the way real erosion does.

attrs.label: Swiss warp
attrs.tooltip:
Swiss only: how far each octave is pushed sideways
by the slope of the one below, which bends the
ridges into something that looks worn rather than
generated.

attrs.label: Cell jitter
attrs.tooltip:
Worley only: how far each cell's point strays from
the middle of its square. 0 is a visible grid; 1 is
scattered.

attrs.label: Wavenumber
attrs.tooltip:
How many times the pattern repeats across the tile,
across and down. Higher is smaller features; the two
differing stretches the pattern one way.

attrs.label: Offset
attrs.tooltip:
Slides the pattern under the terrain. Use it to move a
feature off a spot rather than reaching for a new
seed, which would change everything at once.

attrs.label: Rotation °
attrs.tooltip:
Turns the pattern. Anything with a grain - strata,
dunes, waves - reads very differently across the slope
than along it.

nodes.description: Vue-class fractal: base noise over harmonics with stretch, combination modes, variable roughness, distortion and a filter profile; second output is the local roughness

attrs.label: Base noise
attrs.tooltip:
The pattern repeated at every harmonic. Grainy keeps
detail at all frequencies (colour and bump work).

attrs.label: With rotation
attrs.tooltip:
Rotate the noise between harmonics, so the lattice's
directions never line up.

attrs.label: Double noise
attrs.tooltip:
A second, offset noise multiplied in: richer variation,
about twice the cost.

attrs.label: Filter steepness
attrs.tooltip: Contrast of the base noise itself.

attrs.label: Wavelength
attrs.tooltip: Size of the largest feature, as a fraction of the tile.

attrs.label: Stretch X / Y
attrs.tooltip:
Pulls the pattern out along one axis. Unequal values
give the grain that ridges running one way, or wind-
blown ground, actually has.

attrs.label: Stretch damping
attrs.tooltip:
Less stretch on the finer harmonics, so the whole pattern
does not read as smeared.

attrs.label: Iterations
attrs.tooltip:
How many times the pattern is added to itself at a
smaller size. Each one adds finer detail and costs
about as much again; past the point where an octave
is smaller than a texel it adds cost and nothing
else.

attrs.label: Scale ratio
attrs.tooltip:
Wavelength ratio between iterations. 0.5 is classic;
above favours the large forms, below the fine detail.

attrs.label: Amplitude ratio
attrs.tooltip: Amplitude ratio between iterations.

attrs.label: Roughness
attrs.tooltip: Scales the amplitude ratio: more roughness, more detail.

attrs.label: Gain
attrs.tooltip: Contrast of the result.

attrs.label: Combination mode
attrs.tooltip: How the iterations are put together (manual p866-870).

attrs.label: Smooth level
attrs.tooltip:
Altitude of least roughness; roughness grows with the
distance from it (Variable Roughness Fractal).

attrs.label: Influence
attrs.tooltip: 0 behaves exactly like a simple fractal.

attrs.label: Local influence
attrs.tooltip:
0: keyed on the first iteration's altitude. 1: on the
last iteration's, giving local patches of smoothness.

attrs.label: Variation strength
attrs.tooltip: Grainy fractal: how much the grain varies over the map.

attrs.label: Variation roughness
attrs.tooltip:
How rough the rough areas get, once Influence has
decided where they are. Does nothing while Influence
is zero.

attrs.label: Smooth area altitude
attrs.tooltip:
The height the smooth areas settle to. Below the
Smooth level this lifts them, above it lowers them -
which is how a flat valley floor sits lower than the
broken ground around it.

attrs.label: Distortion
attrs.tooltip: Smears the pattern around, as if pushed by a random flow.

attrs.label: Distortion scale
attrs.tooltip:
How large the smearing flow is. Low values push the
whole pattern about in broad sweeps; high values
ripple its edges without moving the big forms.

attrs.label: Distortion map strength
attrs.tooltip:
The 'distortion map' input, when wired, warps the
coordinates by this much.

attrs.label: Filter
attrs.tooltip: A profile applied to the altitudes (Vue's filter curve).

attrs.label: Terrace steps
attrs.tooltip:
How many levels the Terraces filter snaps altitudes
to. Only the Terraces profile uses it.

attrs.label: Creep-in
attrs.tooltip: How much of the unfiltered signal is mixed back.

attrs.label: Filter range
attrs.tooltip: The part of the full range the filter acts on.

attrs.label: Amplitude
attrs.tooltip:
Scales the whole result. Use it to make one fractal a
quieter contribution when several are added together.

attrs.label: Offset
attrs.tooltip:
Raises or lowers the whole result. Applied after the
amplitude, before the output block below.

attrs.label: Gain

Contrast of the result: pushes the highs up and the
lows down about the middle.

attrs.label: Distortion
attrs.tooltip:
Smears the pattern around as if pushed by a slow flow,

attrs.label: Separate mountains
attrs.tooltip:
On: independent mountain blocks side by side.
Off: basins separated by irregular ridges.

attrs.label: Scale factor
attrs.tooltip:
How much smaller each new iteration's features are,
and how much less they add. This is the whole scale
control for this fractal - it stands in for the

attrs.label: Flat level (per iteration)
attrs.tooltip: Balance of smooth areas against ridged ones per iteration.

attrs.label: Ground level
attrs.tooltip: Sinks the fractal into the ground.

attrs.label: Subdivision quality
attrs.tooltip:
Higher hides the approximation's discontinuities,
at a cost.

attrs.label: Stretch factor
attrs.tooltip:
Each iteration is stretched along its own direction,
the way real ridge networks run.

attrs.label: Optional rocks

attrs.tooltip: Rocks follow the ridges seen at this iteration.

attrs.label: Rock roughness
attrs.tooltip:

attrs.label: Rock height
attrs.tooltip:

nodes.description: Terrain modeling: stamp a heightfield shape onto the terrain

attrs.label: Shape image (if no input)
attrs.tooltip:
The shape to stamp, when nothing is wired to the
shape input. The input wins if both are given.

attrs.label: Position
attrs.tooltip: Where the stamp lands, as a fraction of the tile.

attrs.label: Size
attrs.tooltip: How much of the tile the stamp covers.

attrs.label: Rotation °
attrs.tooltip: Turns the stamp before it is applied.

attrs.label: Height
attrs.tooltip:
How far the stamp raises the ground. Negative
presses it in instead, which is how the same shape
carves a pit or raises a hill.

attrs.label: Blend
attrs.tooltip:
How the stamp meets what is already there. Add sums
them, so stamps pile up. Max merges - the stamp
shows only where it is higher, which is what you
want for laying a hill onto terrain. Min carves.
Replace overwrites wherever the stamp is present.

attrs.label: Edge falloff
attrs.tooltip:
How far in from the stamp's border it fades out, so
it blends into the terrain rather than ending at a
visible square edge.

attrs.label: Invert blend
attrs.tooltip:
Applies this node where the blend input is dark instead of
where it is bright.

Raises or lowers the whole result. Applied after the

attrs.label: Rough areas: ref. feature size
attrs.tooltip:
Harmonics finer than this (fraction of the tile) count
as roughness. 0 counts them all.

attrs.label: Remap to range
attrs.tooltip:
Rescales the result so its lowest point sits at the
bottom of the range below and its highest at the top.

attrs.label: Output range
attrs.tooltip:
