node a gentler contribution when it is added to
another.

attrs.label: Invert
attrs.tooltip:
Turns the result upside down within its range - peaks
become hollows. Applied after the remap.

attrs.label: Gain (gamma)
attrs.tooltip:
Bends the result toward its low or high end. Below 1
lifts the middle, so more of the map sits high; above
1 pushes it down, so peaks become sparser and sharper.

attrs.label: Zero edges width
attrs.tooltip:
Fades the terrain to zero at the borders over this
fraction of the map — clean edges for islands/tiles.

nodes.description: Vue's Terrain Fractal 2: rocks emerging from sedimentary soil, with regions of rock density, soil thickness, buoyancy and relief-following strata

attrs.label: Wavelength
attrs.tooltip:
The size of the largest feature, as a fraction of the
tile. 1 is one landform filling the map; 0.1 is ten
across it.

attrs.label: Iterations
Scale ratio
attrs.tooltip:
How much smaller each iteration is than the last. 0.5
halves it, which is the classic choice; higher leaves a
gap between the scales and reads as two patterns rather
than one surface.

attrs.label: Roughness
attrs.tooltip:
How much strength each iteration keeps. Low is smooth
and dominated by the big forms; high is broken at every
scale.

attrs.label: Gain
attrs.tooltip:
Contrast of the result: pushes the highs up and the
lows down about the middle.

attrs.label: Distortion
attrs.tooltip:
Smears the pattern around as if pushed by a slow flow,
which breaks up the lattice the noise sits on.

attrs.label: Turbulence
attrs.tooltip: Overall distortion of the terrain by its first harmonics.

attrs.label: Turbulence damping
attrs.tooltip:
How much the first octaves' turbulence carries into
the finer ones.

attrs.label: Large scale smoothness
attrs.tooltip:
Softness of the transition from low to high rock
density regions.

attrs.label: Large scale contrast
attrs.tooltip: Range over which the rock population can vary.

attrs.label: Buoyancy
attrs.tooltip:
+: low average altitude with rocks rising above it.
-: features dig below a high average. 0: around zero.

attrs.label: Bump surge
attrs.tooltip: How much the rocks spring out of the ground.

attrs.label: Rock abundance
attrs.tooltip:
How much bare rock emerges through the soil. This
node models ground as rock under sediment, and this
is the balance between them.

attrs.label: Soil thickness
attrs.tooltip:
Thin: more rocks show and smooth areas keep some
roughness. Thick: rocks buried, smooth areas smooth.

attrs.label: Rock dispersion
attrs.tooltip: Scattered over the landscape rather than gathered.

attrs.label: Processing strength
attrs.tooltip:
How strongly bedding shows in the surface. 0 turns
the strata off entirely; the beds follow the relief
rather than lying flat, so they bend over the
landforms the way tilted sediment does.

attrs.label: Layer spacing
attrs.tooltip:
How far apart the beds are, as a fraction of the
height range. Small gives fine banding; large gives
the broad benches of a canyon wall.

attrs.label: Offset
attrs.tooltip:
Slides the whole stack of beds up or down, which
moves where a bed boundary falls on a given slope.

attrs.tooltip:

band-limited - each octave occupies a clean slice of

than turning to mush.

attrs.label: Scale
attrs.tooltip:

tile. Higher is a finer pattern.

attrs.label: Gain
attrs.tooltip:

before. Low leaves the coarse bands dominant; high
gives equal detail at every scale.

nodes.description: Image finishing after tone mapping: exposure, saturation, colour tint

attrs.label: Exposure multiplier
attrs.tooltip: How much light the picture is given, in stops.

attrs.label: Saturation
attrs.tooltip: How strong the colour is in the finished frame.

attrs.label: Tint
attrs.tooltip:
A colour cast over the whole frame - the grade, not the
lighting.

attrs.label: Vignette
attrs.tooltip:
Recorded for the offline post pass; the viewport ignores it for
now (roadmap P6 post-render options).

nodes.description: An HDR image dome at infinity behind the scene, hazed and clouded by the atmosphere

attrs.label: Enabled
attrs.tooltip: Turns the backdrop off without losing its settings.

attrs.label: HDR image (.hdr / .exr / .png / .jpg)
attrs.tooltip:
The panoramic image behind the scene. It lights nothing -
this is what the camera sees past the terrain, not an
environment light.

attrs.label: Mapping
attrs.tooltip:
How pixels map onto directions. Lat-long is what HDRI
libraries ship; a cross is detected as horizontal or
vertical by its aspect; cylindrical and planar use the
vertical field of view below.

attrs.label: Vertical field of view °
attrs.tooltip: Cylindrical panorama and planar backdrop only.

attrs.label: Mirror horizontally
attrs.tooltip:
Mirrors the panorama, for when it was shot or stored the
other way round.

attrs.label: Rotate °
attrs.tooltip:
Turns the backdrop about the vertical, to put its
interesting part behind the shot.

attrs.label: Tilt °
attrs.tooltip:
Tilts the backdrop, to raise or drop its horizon against
the terrain's.

attrs.label: Exposure (EV)
attrs.tooltip:
How bright the backdrop is, in stops. Matching it to the
scene's own exposure is what stops the join being visible.

attrs.label: Tint
attrs.tooltip:
A colour cast over the backdrop alone, for matching it to
the scene's light.

attrs.label: Blend over the sky
attrs.tooltip:
1 replaces the procedural sky with the image; lower values mix.
Where a mapping has no pixel (below a sky dome, outside a planar
backdrop) the procedural sky shows through.

attrs.label: Atmosphere on the dome
attrs.tooltip:
How much horizon haze and fog the dome receives, as if at
infinite distance. Clouds always draw in front of it.

attrs.label: Hide the sun disc
attrs.tooltip: An HDRI usually contains its own sun.

attrs.label: Exposure
attrs.tooltip: How much light the picture is given, in stops.

attrs.label: Terrain height scale
attrs.tooltip:
The terrain's vertical scale, so the render matches what
the viewport shows.

attrs.label: Terrain size (m)
attrs.tooltip:
How wide the tile is in metres, so anything sized in real
units renders at the right size.

nodes.description: Master output: file, format, size, engine and samples of the render

attrs.label: Output file
attrs.tooltip: Where the finished image is written.

attrs.label: Beauty format
attrs.tooltip:
Passes are always written as linear float EXR beside the
beauty, whatever this is.

attrs.label: Width
attrs.tooltip: The width of the rendered image, in pixels.

attrs.label: Height
attrs.tooltip: The height of the rendered image, in pixels.

attrs.label: Engine
attrs.tooltip:
Which renderer produces the frame. The viewport engine is
immediate; the path tracer is slower and resolves real
light transport.

attrs.label: Samples
attrs.tooltip:
How many samples each pixel gets. This is the direct trade
between noise and time - noise falls with the square root,
so four times the samples is half the noise.

nodes.description: Which channels the render writes beside the beauty: depth, normal, id, light, atmosphere...

attrs.label: Depth (metres)
attrs.tooltip:
Writes a linear EXR of distance from the camera to the
surface beside the beauty pass, for compositing.

attrs.label: World normal
attrs.tooltip:
Writes a linear EXR of the direction each surface faces
beside the beauty pass, for compositing.

attrs.label: World position
attrs.tooltip:
Writes a linear EXR of the world position of each surface
point beside the beauty pass, for compositing.

attrs.label: Object id
attrs.tooltip:
Writes a linear EXR of which object each pixel belongs to
beside the beauty pass, for compositing.

attrs.label: Water mask
attrs.tooltip:
Writes a linear EXR of where water covers the frame beside
the beauty pass, for compositing.

attrs.label: Albedo
attrs.tooltip:
Writes a linear EXR of the surface colour with no lighting
on it beside the beauty pass, for compositing.

attrs.label: Direct sun light
attrs.tooltip:
Writes a linear EXR of light arriving straight from a
source beside the beauty pass, for compositing.

attrs.label: Shadow mask
attrs.tooltip:
Writes a linear EXR of where light is blocked beside the
beauty pass, for compositing.

attrs.label: Sky / ambient light
attrs.tooltip:
Writes a linear EXR of light arriving from the sky as a
whole beside the beauty pass, for compositing.

attrs.label: Specular / reflection
attrs.tooltip:
Writes a linear EXR of the highlights alone beside the
beauty pass, for compositing.

attrs.label: Fog & haze (rgb + transmittance)
attrs.tooltip:
Writes a linear EXR of the haze and fog between camera and
surface beside the beauty pass, for compositing.

attrs.label: Sky & backdrop only
attrs.tooltip:
Writes a linear EXR of light arriving from the backdrop
beside the beauty pass, for compositing.

nodes.description: The outline of the ground - rectangle, round, or your own mask - with a wandering rim and an edge that gives way over a distance you set

attrs.label: Shape
attrs.tooltip:
Round is an ellipse when the width and height differ.
From mask takes the outline from the mask input and
only the edge treatment from here.

attrs.label: Size
attrs.tooltip:
Width and height across, as a fraction of the tile. 1
touches the borders; less leaves ground around it.

attrs.label: Centre
attrs.tooltip:
Where the shape sits on the tile. Outside 0..1 pushes
it off the edge, which is how you get a coast rather
than an island.

attrs.label: Rotation
attrs.tooltip:
Turns the shape. Meaningless for a circle, and the whole
point for a stretched one.

attrs.label: Corner rounding
attrs.tooltip:
Rounded rectangle only: how much of the half-size the
corners round off. 1 is a full stadium.

attrs.label: Edge wander
attrs.tooltip:
How far the rim departs from the perfect curve, as a
fraction of the radius. 0 is a drawing-board outline,
which is the one thing no real coast has.

attrs.label: Edge detail
attrs.tooltip: How many bays and headlands there are around the rim.

attrs.label: Edge roughness
attrs.tooltip: How much finer detail rides on the large bays.

attrs.label: Blend extent
attrs.tooltip:
How far in from the rim the blend reaches, as a
fraction of the shape's own radius - so it means the
same on a big island and a small one. 1 blends from
the very centre.

attrs.label: Blend gradient
attrs.tooltip:
The curve from the centre out to the sides. Below 1
the ground stays high and drops away near the rim -
a plateau with a cliff. Above 1 it starts falling
from well inside - a beach. 1 is the plain S-curve.

attrs.label: Blend intensity
attrs.tooltip:
How far down the edge actually goes. 1 takes it all
the way to the base level; less leaves the rim
standing proud of it.

attrs.label: Base level
attrs.tooltip: What the ground outside the shape falls to.

attrs.label: Level
attrs.tooltip: Used when Base level is 'Set below'.

attrs.label: Keep relief outside
attrs.tooltip:
On, the terrain outside keeps its shape and is only
pulled down toward the base - an island on a seabed
that still has hills. Off, outside is flat.

nodes.description: Map height to a color gradient

attrs.label: Gradient
attrs.tooltip: The colour ramp height is looked up in.

attrs.label: Multiply hillshade
attrs.tooltip:
Multiplies the colour by a shaded relief, so the form
reads even where the colours are flat.

nodes.description: Tangent-space normal map from height

attrs.label: Strength
attrs.tooltip:
How strongly the height differences tilt the normal. High
values exaggerate the relief in the shading without moving
any geometry.

nodes.description: Physically-inspired layered terrain albedo

attrs.label: Snow line
attrs.tooltip: The height above which snow lies.

attrs.label: Vegetation ceiling
attrs.tooltip: The height above which vegetation stops.

attrs.label: Rock slope threshold
attrs.tooltip:
How steep the ground must be before bare rock shows
through the soil.

attrs.label: Snow max slope
attrs.tooltip:
How steep the ground may be and still hold snow. Above it
snow slides off, which is what leaves the black rock faces
on a white mountain.

attrs.label: Sand level
attrs.tooltip: The height below which sand appears.

attrs.label: Noise breakup
attrs.tooltip:
How much noise disturbs the boundaries between the
surfaces, so they do not read as contour lines.

attrs.label: Detail scale
attrs.tooltip: How fine the surface detail is.

attrs.label: Flow darkening
attrs.tooltip:
How much the ground darkens where water collects and runs,
which is one of the strongest cues that a terrain has
weather.

attrs.label: Multiply hillshade
attrs.tooltip: Multiplies the colour by a shaded relief.

nodes.description: Drag a mask downstream along the flow

attrs.label: Steps
attrs.tooltip: How many cells downstream each value is carried.

attrs.label: Fade per step
attrs.tooltip:
How much the dragged value weakens at each step
downstream.

attrs.label: Route through pits
attrs.tooltip:
Routes flow through hollows instead of stopping in them,
so a mask carries all the way to the map edge.

attrs.label: Invert blend
attrs.tooltip:
Applies this node where the blend input is dark instead of
where it is bright.

nodes.description: Blend the tile so it wraps seamlessly

attrs.label: Feather
attrs.tooltip:
How much of the tile is blended into its opposite edge.
The wider the blend the more seamless the wrap, and the
more of the original is lost.

attrs.label: Invert blend
attrs.tooltip:
Applies this node where the blend input is dark instead of
where it is bright.

nodes.description: Resynthesize the surface from its own patches

attrs.label: Patch size
attrs.tooltip:
How large the patches taken from the source are, as a
fraction of the tile. Large patches keep more of the
original's structure; small ones mix more freely and
repeat less.

attrs.label: Overlap
attrs.tooltip:
As a fraction of the patch. Wider overlaps hide seams
better and repeat more.

attrs.label: Candidates
attrs.tooltip:
Patches auditioned per cell; the best-matching overlap
wins. More candidates, better joins, slower quilt.

attrs.label: Invert blend
attrs.tooltip:
Applies this node where the blend input is dark instead of
where it is bright.

nodes.description: Pin the tile's borders to a level

attrs.label: Border level
attrs.tooltip: The height the borders are pinned to.

attrs.label: Feather
attrs.tooltip:
How far in from the border the pinning reaches, so the
terrain eases to it rather than dropping at the edge.

attrs.label: Invert blend
attrs.tooltip:
Applies this node where the blend input is dark instead of

nodes.description: Directional rock shearing / folding (Gaea-style)

attrs.tooltip: How large the shear bands are.

attrs.label: Shear amount
attrs.tooltip: How far the rock is displaced along the shear.

attrs.label: Folding
attrs.tooltip:
How much the sheared rock folds back on itself rather than
simply sliding.

attrs.label: Direction °
attrs.tooltip: Which way the shearing acts.

attrs.label: Self modulated
attrs.tooltip:
Height drives shear strength — bands show on
slopes, flats stay intact.

attrs.label: Invert blend

nodes.description: Translate / scale / rotate

attrs.tooltip: Slides the terrain across the tile.

attrs.label: Scale
attrs.tooltip: Zooms the terrain in or out, across and down separately.

attrs.label: Rotate °
attrs.tooltip: Rotates the terrain.

attrs.label: Outside area
attrs.tooltip:
What fills the ground the transform has moved away from.
Clamp smears the border outward, mirror reflects it, tile
repeats the map - which only looks right if the terrain
was seamless to begin with.

attrs.label: Invert blend
attrs.tooltip:
Applies this node where the blend input is dark instead of

attrs.tooltip: Which way the terrain is dragged.

attrs.label: Amplitude
attrs.tooltip: How far it is dragged.

attrs.label: Scale by height
attrs.tooltip:
On, the high ground is dragged further than the low, so
peaks lean over and reads as wind-shaped or as material
having slumped. Off, the whole map shifts together.

attrs.label: Invert blend
attrs.tooltip:
Applies this node where the blend input is dark instead of

nodes.description: Domain warp by internal fBm noise

attrs.label: Amplitude
attrs.tooltip:
How far the terrain is pushed sideways. Warping the
coordinates rather than the heights is what turns a
regular pattern into something organic - the lattice the
noise sits on stops being visible.

attrs.label: Warp frequency
attrs.tooltip:
How large the warping swirls are, across and down. Low
values sweep the whole map about; high ones ripple its
edges.

attrs.label: Octaves
attrs.tooltip:
How many scales of warping are layered. More gives a more
intricately folded result.

attrs.label: Invert blend
attrs.tooltip:
Applies this node where the blend input is dark instead of
where it is bright.
